When I joined APF, I said we wanted to do 26 1/2-minute programs. I don't think we can do that. We may be lucky to do 24 shows each season. I think in addition to 26 1/2-minute programs we should do 13 programs of 13 1/2 minutes each. That's the only way to have a full season.
The first 26 @-@ episode, "The Constitution: The Home of the Brave," ran on June 17, 1969. The series was designed to enhance the show's prestige among its target audience of high school seniors, and it was clear from the outset that the episodes would be more accessible than APF 's standard fare. APF 's former director of research and development, John T. Davis, defined the series's goal as follows:
The idea was to create a program for the high school student—a program that was written with him in mind, that was attractive to him, that was relevant to his life. And to write a program that would be of some value to the teacher, as well.
A 1969 APF newsletter stated that the program would "promote humanistic, social, and political understanding" among its viewers. Indeed, the program was designed to be a comprehensive educational experience that would provide its audience with a "general orientation through the humanities, the social sciences, and the arts."
In its first season, _26 @-@_ presented segments on such topics as the American presidency ("Presidential Campaigns"), the U.S. Constitution ("The Constitution: The Home of the Brave"), the history of the American family ("The American Family"), the history of jazz ("Jazz"), the history of the American personal computer ("The Personal Computer"), the Civil War ("The Civil War"), and the WPA murals in Golden Gate Park ("The WPA Murals").
The program featured a cast of well-known performers and actors, including 1960s icons Lee Grant, Pat Swayze, and Beau Bridges, along with more familiar names like Jan Murray, Leslie Uggams, and Don Murray. In an interview in 2006, Don Murray remembered the experience of performing on _26 @-@_ fondly:

Nault, who coached one of Hamels's youth baseball teams, recalls that Hamels was a pitcher-shortstop in youth recreational baseball. "I knew he liked baseball," Nault says. Hamels, who had played quarterback for four years, was 6'4", 205 pounds when he entered high school. He was strong, but his coordination wasn't great. Nault's job as a tee ball coach was to get the kids to bat and field properly and to teach them the basics of the game. He didn't want to overload the children with the details of baseball. "I just wanted them to learn how to play the game," he says. "I knew that Cole was going to be a pitcher. But baseball was still something I always wanted to do. I liked having a team. Hamels's father, Steve, was an assistant football coach at the high school and became a baseball coach in the summer. He coached the team with Nault. "I'm a baseball guy," Nault says. "I was a catcher in high school. I coached travel ball. I played in the Cape Cod League. I've been involved in baseball my whole life."
In the offseason, Hamels would come to the school's baseball field and lift weights, do agility drills, and take ground balls with Coach Nault. They'd throw and catch. The work paid off in terms of Hamels's baseball skills. Nault also says that "what I didn't realize was that Cole's body was changing. He was becoming a man."
Hamels's father, Steve, says that his son was "not a very big kid" when he entered high school. That changed fast. ( Sergent şi subofiţeri )  and recruits ( Recruţi ). Each branch has a different composition of these four grades. These ranks are also used by the Romanian Air Force , and the Romanian Navy .
The word Sergent is also used to address a person of superior rank , in a commanding way . In this case, the person uttering the word is referred to as "Sergent" ( Sergent-Maior or Sergent-Mareşal  for an officer or Sergent major or Sergent maior for a warrant officer ) .
Both the Army and the Air Force have a brigade ( Brigăză ) rank, while the Navy only has a division ( Divizie ) rank.
The ranks of the Romanian Land Forces are organized in a hierarchy system that is similar to that of the European armies. There are four main ranks : officer , warrant officer , noncommissioned officer (NCO) , and recruit .

In 1894 the Little Rock Æsthetic Club , one of the oldest women 's societies west of the Mississippi River , moved into the Tow

ers Building at 5th and Markham (now Cumberland) in Little Rock, Arkansas. The club spent $10,000 on the building, which was previously the home of Little Rock s Presbyterian Church . In 1892 the Little Rock Æsthetic Club had also loaned $15,000 to the Presbyterian Church to pay off the remaining debt on the church building. The Little Rock Æsthetic Club also owned the old Methodist Church building at the corner of 7th and Scott. The Æsthetics were the first women's club, not only in Little Rock but also in Arkansas.
The club was organized on February 13, 1869, with Mrs. Roe as president, Mrs. W. Q. Wilson as vice-president, Mrs. Levi Collier as secretary, and Mrs. John W. Martin as treasurer. The club originally met in the home of Mrs. Roe, but the meetings were moved to the old Presbyterian Church building when the Æsthetics purchased their building in 1894. The Æsthetics were the first women's club in Little Rock, although the first women's club in Arkansas was the Woman's Club of Little Rock (1877). The club was named the Æsthetic Club because the members "practiced æsthetics, or the art of creating beauty."
The Æsthetics were primarily concerned with social affairs, including some of the first art exhibitions in Little Rock. They were also active in philanthropic activities, especially in the area of education. In 1876 the Æsthetics began a school for African-American children, which was closed in 1920. They also established a scholarship fund to help girls from the Southwest School for Girls (now Little Rock Central High School) continue their education.
In 1908 the club decided to disband. However, the charter of the club was approved by the Arkansas Woman Suffrage Association in 1910. In 1916 the club was organized under the new name of the Æsthetic Club of Arkansas. The club is still in existence.

They were joined by the kings of France and Scotland , and the king of Castile .
In 1179 , Henry was reconciled with the Church, and he set out for a crusade in 1180 . He returned to England in 1182 , and he was crowned again in the same year. The next day, the cyclone began to develop, and the Joint Typhoon Warning Center ( JTWC ) designated the system as 99W. The next day, the Japan Meteorological Agency ( JMA ) issued advisories on the system, and the JTWC issued advisories on the same day, designating the system as a tropical depression. The JTWC upgraded the system to tropical storm status the next day and the JMA followed suit two hours later. A few hours later, the JTWC upgraded the system to typhoon status, and the JMA followed suit the next day.
On September 2, the typhoon made landfall on Guam, but the weather conditions were too bad for the JTWC to send weather reconnaissance aircraft in to survey the storm. The storm strengthened as it made its way through the Philippine Sea, and on September 3, the JTWC upgraded the system to super typhoon status. The JMA followed suit the next day and the JTWC upgraded the storm to their highest classification, Category 5-equivalent, the next day. The JMA continued to upgrade the storm to Category 4-equivalent on September 4. The storm strengthened to peak winds of 180 mph (290 km/h) the next day, making the storm the strongest in the Northwestern Pacific since 2001.
The typhoon started to weaken as it approached Taiwan, but it strengthened as it approached China. On September 11, the JTWC issued their last advisory on the storm. The JMA issued their last advisory on the storm the next day, and the JTWC issued their last advisory on September 12.

It caused 21 deaths in Guam, 2 in Japan, and eight in China. The storm will go down in history as one of the worst typhoons ever to affect the northern Philippines.

The Lotus 79 was the first Formula One car to use a ground effect aerodynamic system, although the idea had been used in midget racing cars since the 1970s. 

The 1978 Italian Grand Prix was the 32nd running of the Italian Grand Prix and the seventh round of the 1978 Formula One season. The race, held on 10 September 1978, was held at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza in Monza, Italy. The race was held in wet conditions. The race was won by Lotus driver Mario Andretti, the first of his three victories in Formula One. It was also the first Lotus victory since 1975. Didier Pironi finished second in his Ligier–Renault, while fellow Frenchman Jacques Laffite finished third in a Ligier–Matra.

## Background

The Italian Grand Prix event was held at the Monza Circuit in Italy. The 1978 season was the 32nd season of the Formula One championship. 

The season was marked by several accidents that necessitated safety improvements at circuits. At the Dutch Grand Prix in May, a trackside catch fence was breached when the Ligier of Jacques Laffite crashed into it at high speed. Laffite was injured but survived the accident. The accident provoked a media uproar and the Italian Grand Prix was run under contract for the first time. 

## Qualifying

Pole position was shared by Gilles Villeneuve (left) and Eddie Cheever (right), with the former setting a new track record.

Qualifying was held on 9 September. The pole position was secured by Gilles Villeneuve, who set a new track record, by 0.3 seconds.

## Race

The race was held on 10 September. Rain fell on the circuit during the race. After the start of the race, Villeneuve led the race from start to finish, but his Renault suffered a brake failure shortly before the finish. He crashed into the barriers, but was unhurt. Didier Pironi, who started the race from second, inherited the lead, but also crashed out of the race, after being involved in a collision with Jacques Laffite. Mario Andretti inherited the lead and won the race, the first of his three victories in Formula One. Both Andretti and Laffite finished on the podium. This was the first Lotus victory since 1975.

Arsenal's title win was the first time in Premier League history that the title race went to the last day of the season, and also the first time that the title was won by a team that had not been champions in the previous season.

Newly promoted Wimbledon were relegated at the end of the season, along with Charlton Athletic, Derby County and Blackburn Rovers.

The conference was a key event in the development of A.I. research, and the term " artificial intelligence " was coined by McCarthy. The conference was sponsored by Dartmouth College's Computer Research Center, IBM, and the National Science Foundation .
While crossing the mountainous terrain of Hispaniola , Katie became very disorganized and rapidly weakened to a tropical storm

off the coast of Cuba on October 14. In a brief period of reorganization, Katie rapidly strengthened into a hurricane on October 16 as it moved through the Yucatan Channel. The intensification came to a halt on October 17, and by October 18, Katie had weakened to a tropical depression. Katie killed a total of 38 people in Haiti , and caused $47 million (1998 USD, $70.5 million 2010 USD) in damage.
Katie was the seventh named storm to occur in the 1998 Atlantic hurricane season. Katie's name was retired from the list of Atlantic tropical cyclone names, and was replaced by Katia in the 2003 season.
 A tropical wave emerged from the African coast on October 9. Traveling westward, it moved into the Caribbean Sea on October 11. A low pressure area developed from the wave on October 12, and the next day, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) classified the system as Tropical Depression Seven. The depression slowly intensified, and on October 14, the NHC upgraded it to Tropical Storm Katie. On October 14, Katie's maximum sustained winds remained at 45 mph (72 km/h), and its minimum pressure was 1006 mbar (hPa; 29.7 inHg).
Katie began to rapidly weaken as it moved over Hispaniola, and on October 15, the NHC downgraded Katie to a tropical depression. Early on October 16, Katie began to weaken again, and the NHC downgraded Katie to a tropical depression. On October 17, Katie weakened to a tropical depression. Katie moved through the Yucatan Channel, and on October 18, the NHC downgraded Katie to a tropical depression. Katie moved into the Gulf of Mexico, and on October 19, the NHC downgraded it to a tropical depression. On October 20, Katie dissipated about 110 mi (180 km) southeast of Galveston, Texas.
 Overall, Katie caused $47 million (1998 USD, $70.5 million 2010 USD) in damage. It killed 38 people in Haiti.

With a mass only 80 times that of Jupiter ( MJ ) , 2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403 is the smallest known star undergoing nuclear fusion in

its core. This star is only 400 light years away, but it is bright enough to be seen with the naked eye in the northern hemisphere in a clear sky away from city lights. For an object of this mass, it is the fourth faintest. Its surface temperature is about 3,500 K. This star has been found to be a member of the Ursa Major moving group.
2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403 has the distinction of being the first star to be discovered by the All-Sky Survey released by the 2 Micron All Sky Survey. It was discovered as part of their search for objects that were not main sequence stars, and thus might be good candidates for being a brown dwarf.
This star is surrounded by a faint halo of gas and dust 120 ly across. This is more than three times the distance from the Sun to the nearest major planet.
This object has a highly variable brightness. The variability is too large to be caused by an eclipsing binary or pulsations.
2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403 has been found to have a small companion.
2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403 was discovered by the All-Sky Survey in 1997.
The star has several proper names. It is known as TZ Crateris, Kappa Ursae Majoris, or 2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403.
TZ Crateris is the Bayer designation.
Kappa Ursae Majoris is the Flamsteed designation.
2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403 is a variable star.
2MASS J0523 @-@ 1403 has been found to be a member of the Ursa Major moving group.
The explosive charges in HMS Campbeltown detonated at noon on 28 March 1942 , and the dry dock was destroyed . Reports vary on

the exact number killed, but it was in the hundreds, with many more wounded.  The Campbeltown had been under the command of Lt. Cmdr. James St. G. Saunders, a veteran of the Norwegian campaign , who had already received the DSO for his participation in the raid on the Tirpitz.
The Campbeltown was home to a number of American servicemen, and a number of them escaped the explosion because they were on leave at the time of the raid. However , one American, Norman Jackson, the boatswain's mate, was killed in the explosion.
The Campbeltown was bombed and sunk by the Luftwaffe on 19 October 1942.
The Campbeltown is the only Royal Navy vessel to have been intentionally sunk as a blockship.
James St.G. Saunders, commander of the Campbeltown, was awarded the Distinguished Service Order for his participation in the raid on the Tirpitz.

The game 's battle system , the BliTZ system , is carried over directly from Valkyira Chronicles . During missions , players se

ize control of a single character and are tasked with completing objectives. Battle breaks down into two parts. In the first part, players attack the enemy's party until their health is depleted and they are defeated. During the second part, the player's party takes turns attacking the enemy in a turn-based format. While a player's character is attacked, they are given a power gauge that gradually fills as they take damage. The power gauge can then be used to unleash attacks against the enemy. The power gauge's max capacity is determined by the player's BliTZ gauge, which is filled when they deal damage to enemies. When the power gauge is full, all of the player's party members' power gauges are also filled. If a party member runs out of health during a battle, they are unable to attack until their health is fully restored. During stages where the player is attacked by an enemy, the player is given an option to counterattack. If the enemy's attack is blocked, the player is granted an attack point and can counterattack with their own attack.
Players are able to switch between characters at any time. Each character has their own set of attacks and abilities. As the player progresses through the game, the characters' abilities evolve, allowing them to unleash more powerful attacks. The game features an item system that allows the player to equip items to their characters. The items can be used to recover HP, grant stat buffs, and more.

Fish describes the game 's changes during development as " organic " — they tested different kinds of levels and replicated the

best ones. There are limitations on the number of times you can use certain abilities, and it is up to you to figure out how you want to use them. One of the main points of the game is to collect the pieces of a mysterious puzzle, which once constructed will lead to a final confrontation with the game's main antagonist, Gargantua.
The game's structure is nonlinear, allowing the player to choose which level to play. The game's puzzles are "spatial" in nature, requiring players to move the tiles to create forms such as bridges, ladders, and ramps. Fish described the game as " a game about creating, not destroying ", and as having a " circular, cyclical structure ". We're going to have to guide players through that process, but we're not going to be giving them explicit instructions.

Galveston is a beachfront city on Galveston Island and Pelican Island in the U.S. state of Texas. The community of 47,447 is the county seat and second-largest municipality of Galveston County , and for many years was one of the three most important ports in Texas .
Galveston's 1911 legislative charter gave the city a home rule charter , which was repealed in 1989, when the city switched to a council-manager government. Galveston is a resort city with an estimated 1,532 hotel rooms and over 200 restaurants. Galveston Island State Park , located on the east end of Galveston Island, is a popular tourist destination.
Galveston is home to the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston (UTMB), which includes the John Sealy Hospital , and Texas A&M University at Galveston , which houses the Texas Maritime Academy .
Galveston's modern economy is centered in the tourism , health care , shipping , and financial industries. As the Missouri drains a predominantly semi @-@ arid region , its discharge is much lower and more variable than other North Am

erican rivers of comparable size. In the average Missouri , there is less than 1000 cfs at St Louis , and its low flow is generally less than 300 cfs.
The low flow of the Missouri has been known to cause flood problems downstream in the Mississippi valley. Although the flows in the Missouri itself are low, the flows in its tributaries are generally much higher. The Missouri's own discharge is also highly variable, a result of its long distance from the source of precipitation. Its flow is high in the spring and fall and low in the summer.
The Missouri River drains an area of 1.2 million square miles, of which 340,000 square miles is in the United States. Of this area, 168,000 is in Missouri, 48,000 is in Iowa, 39,000 is in Nebraska, 36,000 is in South Dakota, 33,000 is in North Dakota, 26,000 is in Montana, and 23,000 is in Kansas. Its total basin area is greater than the combined basin areas of the Mississippi, the Ohio, and the St Lawrence. The Missouri River is the longest river that flows into the Gulf of Mexico.
The Missouri River has a total length of 2,341 miles. It originates in the Rocky Mountains of southwestern Montana, where it is known as the Jefferson or Madison Rivers. It flows east to the Yellowstone River at Fort Benton, Montana. Below Fort Benton it is known as the Missouri River, and it flows generally southeast through the states of Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, and Kansas. Below Kansas, it flows generally south to join the Mississippi River at St Louis, Missouri.
The Missouri has a drainage area of 481,300 square miles, of which 168,000 is in Missouri. This represents 27.4% of the total drainage area of the United States. The Missouri River is the seventh largest river in the world in terms of drainage area, and the largest river in the United States. The next largest rivers in the United States are the Mississippi (31%), the St Lawrence (10%), the Colorado (9%), the Yukon (7%), and the Yukon-Kuskokwim (6%).
The Missouri River is about 75 miles long in Missouri. Three of its principal tributaries are the Platte, the Kansas, and the Kansas City.
The Missouri River was known to the Spanish and French as the River of the Assiniboines. The name was later changed to the Missouri in honor of the Missouri tribe.
The Missouri River is navigable in its lower 1,600 miles. Its main channel is 230 miles long.
The Missouri River is the source of great quantities of hydroelectric energy. At Fort Benton, Montana, the power potential of the Missouri is 20,000 kilowatts. At Oacoma, South Dakota, it is 19,000 kilowatts. At Fort Peck, Montana, the power potential is 2,400,000 kilowatts, and at Gavins Point, Nebraska, it is 4,000,000 kilowatts.
The Missouri River is home to several species of fish, including the white bass, the sauger, the carp, the catfish, and the sturgeon.
Most of the Missouri River is controlled by a series of dams. The largest of these, in terms of storage capacity, is the Fort Peck Dam, near Fort Peck, Montana. The Fort Peck Dam has a storage capacity of 24,320,000 acre-feet.
The Missouri River is dammed in Missouri at Sioux City, Missouri. The Missouri River is dammed in Iowa at Oacoma and at Sioux City.
The Missouri River is dammed in Nebraska at Omaha and at Gavins Point.
The Missouri River is dammed in South Dakota at Fort Randall and at Gavins Point.
The Missouri River is dammed in North Dakota at Garrison Dam and at Fort Stevenson.

The writer of the scenario is unknown , but it was most likely Lloyd Lonergan . He was an experienced newspaperman employed by

the _Morning Bulletin_ in Rockhampton, Queensland, and the author of a number of scenarios for QFNS.4
The scenario was published in the _Training Manual_ of the Queensland Fire Brigade just after the Second World War.5  It is a 'rescue' scenario, where the fire brigade has to rescue a number of people trapped in a theatre, as well as putting out the fire itself.
This scenario is a typical example of the type of scenario used for fire brigade training in the early period of the NSW fire brigades. The scenario is very similar to two others we have discovered, both of which are for the NSW Fire Brigade. They are also both written by Lloyd Lonergan, who was a journalist for the Sydney _Telegraph_ , and were published in the _Training Manual_ of the NSW Fire Brigade.6  For the purposes of this book, the three scenarios are also closely linked, because they use similar types of fire equipment, and members of the brigades involved in training and fighting fires in the 1920s and 1930s had a great deal of contact with each other, and with the NSW Fire Brigade.7  They also all use the terms 'dummy' and 'blind-fold' in the same way, which I will explain.
There is also a close connection between this scenario and the previous one (Part 1) from the NSW Fire Brigade. In that scenario, there was a fire in a pub, and the fire brigade had to rescue a number of people from the pub, as well as putting out the fire. There was also a theatrical owner, who was tied up, and who was rescued at the end of the scenario. This scenario also has a number of people trapped in a theatre, and a theatrical owner who is tied up. In both cases, the theatrical owner is rescued at the end of the scenario.
In the scenario, there are a number of fire extinguishers available for the fire brigade, and the fire is described as a 'small' fire. The scenario also describes a 'dummy' and 'blind-fold' fire. These terms were used to refer to types of fire, and were not as we use them today, to describe a dummy fire-fighter.8  The term 'dummy' refers to a fire that was lit to test a fire-fighting appliance, such as a dry powder extinguisher or an aerial ladder. The term 'blind-fold' referred to a fire that was lit to test a fire fighting team.9  This is the only time that these terms were used in this way.

On 10 December , three Canadian battalions made their first attempt to cross The Gully . Although they succeeded in capturing V

imy Ridge, they paid a high price. On 11 December , the 21st, 22nd and 24th Battalions suffered almost 2,300 casualties in the attempt.
Looking southeast toward Vimy Ridge from the ravine bottom. The embankment in front of the hedgerow is where the 21st Battalion was hit with machine-gun fire on 10 December.
One of the 21st Battalion's most notable heroes of the battle for Vimy Ridge was its young commander, Lieutenant-Colonel (temporary) William S. Roberts. Born in England, Roberts enlisted in the Canadian Expeditionary Force in England, serving as an officer in the 1st Battalion of the Royal Scots. While serving in the trenches, he was reportedly struck by a German shell fragment, which damaged his right eye. As a result, he was evacuated to a British hospital and, in February , recovered enough to return to his unit.
On 10 May 1915, Roberts was appointed to command the 1st Battalion of the 1st Infantry Brigade. In August , he was promoted to temporary captain and, in mid-October , was appointed to command the 21st Battalion, a unit made up of reinforcements from the 2nd, 4th and 5th Infantry Brigades.
On the morning of 10 December , his battalion was supporting the 24th Battalion as it attempted to capture the Ridge. In the early stages of the attack, Roberts was directing the movement of his battalion along the route they planned to take to the Ridge. As his unit approached the German front line, they were hit by heavy machine-gun and rifle fire.
The 21st Battalion was forced to take cover in a deep ravine and was pinned down for three hours. When his battalion was finally able to advance, it was forced to take cover again by intense fire from the German machine guns. After a few moments, Roberts ordered his unit to advance again, this time up the hill toward Vimy Ridge.
As the battalion was moving forward, Roberts was shot through the face and neck. Incredibly, he was able to remain in command of his battalion until he collapsed. The wounds he received were ultimately fatal and Roberts died three days later.
His body was laid to rest in the Ansdell Valley Cemetery, located just northeast of the village of Givenchy. In 1934, his body was exhumed and re-interred in the Vimy Memorial.
The following is an excerpt from his Victoria Cross citation.
"For most conspicuous bravery and devotion to duty in attack.
Facing the enemy's fire, he led his battalion up the trench and, with the aid of bombing parties, captured the trench.
Later, he directed the consolidation of the trench and held on to it in spite of heavy casualties. He was finally shot through the face and neck and died within a few minutes."
The 21st Battalion's advance up Vimy Ridge on 10 December was led by its second-in-command, Major George F.S. Stevenson.
Stevenson was born in Clifton Hill, Ontario, and enlisted in the 21st Battalion in Kingston, Ontario. In the spring of 1915, he was appointed to command its 14th Company and, shortly thereafter, was promoted to temporary captain. He was appointed adjutant of the battalion in September , with the rank of major.
As the battalion was advancing up Vimy Ridge, its commander was shot and killed. Stevenson took over command and led his unit to the top of the Ridge. In the process, he was shot through the chest.
Stevenson was taken to a dressing station and, although his wounds were serious, he was well enough to return to his unit.
His wounds ultimately forced him to return to Canada. He was discharged from the army in January 1916 and returned to his family in Kingston. Stevenson died in 1971 and was buried in Cataraqui Cemetery.

After the Commando headquarters group had landed , Commander Ryder went to check for himself that Campbeltown was firmly stuck

on the ground. He took with him Captain Miller, Major Nitschke and Captain Rutherford. When they walked to the end of the runway, they saw that the whole of the camp was well lit and the Germans were obviously at their last meal.
At the side of the runway were many tents and huts. There was a large mast which rose from the centre of the camp. This was the wireless station and the transmitting antennae were strung from the mast to the ground. Standing around the mast were a number of Germans.
Nitschke and Miller walked over to the tents. The Germans didn't seem to be paying any attention to them.
Captain Rutherford went to the edge of the camp. The Germans did not appear to be paying any attention to him, either. He walked along the edge of the camp, looking into the huts. He came to a large windowless building which had an open door. He could see that it contained a number of canvas bunks. It was a billet for the radar operators.
The Germans were still unaware of the presence of the Commando party.
Ryder and Rutherford joined Captain Miller and Major Nitschke. They had inspected the camp thoroughly, and had seen no signs of Germans other than the men at the wireless station.
They walked back towards the L.C.I., and saw that the Germans had finished their meal and were now standing around their lorries and vehicles.
Rutherford and the others returned to the L.C.I.
Five minutes later, Ryder, Nitschke, Miller and Rutherford were back on the beach. They decided to wait there until the Germans had stopped playing tennis and gone to bed.
11.30 p.m.
The Germans had finished their game of tennis. They had now gone to bed.
Rutherford decided to return to the L.C.I. to tell Ryder that they were now ready to move the L.C.I. and the L.C.T.s onto the jetty.
11.45 p.m.
Rutherford returned to the L.C.I. He told Ryder that they were now ready to move the L.C.I. and the L.C.T.s onto the jetty.
Ryder told him to get ready to move the L.C.I. and the L.C.T.s onto the jetty at 12.30 a.m.
12.00 a.m.
Major Nitschke and Lieutenant Fraser went to the L.C.I. to make sure that the L.C.I. was ready to move. The L.C.I. had been less damaged than the L.C.T.s. It was ready to be moved onto the jetty.
12.30 a.m.
Major Nitschke gave the order to move the L.C.I. onto the jetty.
The L.C.I. was moved off the beach and onto the jetty.
12.45 a.m.
The L.C.I. was in position on the jetty. Ryder, Nitschke and Fraser boarded the L.C.I. The L.C.I. cast off and moved away from the jetty.
12.47 a.m.
The L.C.I. was safely out of the harbour.
12.50 a.m.
The L.C.T.s were ready to move onto the jetty.
12.52 a.m.

illion people engaged in weaving. It is a symbol of Muslim pride and community identity. Weavers of Varanasi are also well known for their skill. It is believed that the very first weavers of Varanasi were the Brahmins. Muslims are the dominant community in this city, and their community pride is often expressed through weaving. There is a visible link between weaving and Muslim identity. The weavers are involved in the process right from the point of collecting the raw material from the fields. At the same time the weaving is mostly done in the homes of weavers. In this way the entire process of weaving is a source of identity and pride for the community.
In 1969, I was posted to Varanasi for a year as a medical officer, and it was during this period that I became interested in the artistry of Varanasi silk weavers and the process of silk weaving. The weavers are the most courteous and hospitable people I have ever met. They have a popular saying ' _kale ke bachche me_ ' ( _kale_ means the weaving shuttle). Weavers are the children of the shuttle. The weaving shuttle is a bamboo rod with a small piece of silk woven into it. It is thrown up and down the length of the loom and weaves the warp and weft threads into a fabric. The shuttle is a very small part of the loom, but the weaver's fingers and mind are linked to it. It is this link that makes the weaver the child of the shuttle.
The silk weavers of Varanasi are also very proud of their tradition. They feel that they are the descendants of the Brahmins, and their pride in their community is expressed in the songs they sing and the stories they tell. The songs and stories are related to silk weaving, and they are the source of inspiration for the weavers.
Weavers are divided into different categories according to their skill and status. The highest category is that of _khadiya_ , and the lowest category is that of _naiya_ ( _nai_ means a slave). The khadiyas are the first in the hierarchy of weavers. They are the best weavers and the richest of the lot. Their families are the most influential, and their marriages are the most expensive. The khadiyas are also the most organized. They have an association and meet regularly to discuss their problems and share their experiences. They have a central place in the society and are at the top of the hierarchy.
The second category of weavers is that of the _khatadar_ (cloth merchant). These people are the middlemen between the weavers and the market. They purchase the raw material from the weavers and sell it to the shopkeepers. They also arrange the sale of the finished product to the customers. The cloth merchant is the most important person in the hierarchy of weavers and is the most influential in the society.
The third category of weavers is that of the _machi_ (weaver). This category includes all the weavers who do not fall into the categories of khatadar or khadiya. They are considered to be the least important in the hierarchy of weavers. They are usually not very rich and do not have much influence in the society.
The fourth category of weavers is that of the _bahu-kutar_ (cloth-cutter). These people are the lowest in the hierarchy of weavers. They are the most poor and the least influential in the society.

The Dutch painter Gerard van Honthorst (also known as Gherardd de Honthorst or Gherardo delle Notti)  (1592 in Utrecht - 1656 in Rome) is the main subject of this study.
The sources for the thesis are artworks of Honthorst himself, descriptions by contemporary and later writers, and biographical data.
The thesis is concluded with a section on the influence of the works and ideas of Honthorst on the work of Busch.

The work of Gerard van Honthorst (1592-1656) was commissioned by the most important and wealthiest families of the Dutch Republic (1609-1702), including the Van Cuyck, Van Ewes and Van Rechteren families.
His work was widely known in the Netherlands, and continues to be sought after in the Netherlands and abroad.
Honthorst was the most important and influential Dutch Golden Age painter, not only in the Netherlands but also in Italy, particularly in Rome.
His career was cut short when he was only 63 years old.
The present thesis is the first to analyze the work of Gerard van Honthorst, and to show the influence of his work on the work of Busch.
In the second chapter the biography of Honthorst is elaborated, with a special focus on his early years in Rome.
The third chapter discusses the influences on Honthorst, which are attested in his work by his choice of subjects, themes and artistic style.
In the fourth chapter, Honthorst's work as portrait artist is discussed.
Honthorst's own descriptions of his work as a portrait painter are evaluated, and the influence of his work and thoughts on the work of Rembrandt is discussed.
The fifth chapter explains the impact Honthorst had on the work of Busch, who had been influenced by Hals and Rembrandt.
In the sixth chapter, the thesis is summarized and discussed.

He also worked to expand the city's network of urban farms, including a farm in the city's Bromo Tower Arts & Entertainment District, but his first attempt at a food-loop program, which would have used a network of refrigerated trucks to gather excess food from city restaurants and stores and then distribute it to food banks, was defeated in the Maryland State Senate . O'Malley increased the city's minimum wage to $10.10 an hour, and he temporarily suspended paying city contractors in full until the city's fiscal crisis was resolved.
In June 2010, O'Malley announced that he would not run for a third term as mayor. During his tenure, O'Malley was criticized for providing too little funding for neighborhood schools and not addressing the city's budget problems. In an interview with _The Baltimore Sun_ , O'Malley defended his record, saying that he had "always been a builder, not a tearer-down."
O'Malley announced his candidacy for the Democratic nomination for governor of Maryland on January 21, 2011, in Baltimore 's Patterson Park. O'Malley had previously served as a county councilman and mayor of Baltimore before winning the nearby state's governorship in 2006. Though he had been considered a potential candidate for president, O'Malley's 2011 campaign was said to be a "career-defining moment" for him. O'Malley was a strong supporter of same-sex marriage, and had signed the Maryland Family Protection Act in 2012 to recognize same-sex marriages performed in other states.

Brown to become a "virtual lock" to win the Democratic nomination. O'Malley's announcement came after he struggled with low poll numbers and faced criticism for his handling of the state's escalating violent crime rate.
O'Malley cited a desire to spend more time with his family as the reason for dropping out of the race. He also said that he wanted to run for president, and that he would consider running for US senator (a post that his campaign manager claimed he would seek) or perhaps even the vice presidency in 2016. Thomas Cromwell was an English statesman and a close adviser to the king, Henry VIII. He was born in Putney, then in Surrey , but later in his life was declared a citizen of London. He was the son of Walter Cromwell, a merchant tailor of Putney who was involved in the cloth trade.

James VI and I was King of Scots as James VI from 24 July 1567 and King of England and Ireland as James I from the union of the English and Scottish crowns on 24 March 1603 until his death on 27 March 1625. George, Prince of Wales, was the eldest son of King George II and Queen Caroline of Ansbach, both members of the House of Hanover , and heir apparent to the throne of Great Britain from 1727.
The English Civil War , often called the Civil War in England , was a series of armed conflicts and political machinations that took place between Parliamentarians and Royalists. The first outbreak was in August 1642 and the war concluded almost exactly 11 years later in May 1651.
The English Restoration was the political restoration of the English monarchy and of English monarchical government, following the Interregnum that occurred after the execution of King Charles I in 1649. Commonly known as the Reformation, it was a movement that changed religion in England from being part of the Roman Catholic Church to being part of the Protestant Reformation and the Anglican Communion.
The Great Fire of London was a major conflagration that swept through the central parts of the English city of London, from Sunday, 2 September to Thursday, 6 September 1666. The fire gutted the medieval City of London within the old Roman city wall. It threatened but did not reach the City of Westminster, Charles II's ceremonial centre, and it gutted most of the medieval parish of St. Giles on the north side of the City. It destroyed the homes of 70,000 of the City's 80,000 inhabitants. The death toll is unknown but estimates range from 6 to 7,000. The majority of those who died were homeless, destitute refugees from their homes.

Humpty Dumpty has been used to demonstrate the second law of thermodynamics . The law describes a process known as entropy , a

measure of the disorder within a system. As an egg, it is a closed, self-contained system. The eggs and Humpty Dumpty inside are in a coherent, ordered state, with a low entropy level. When Humpty Dumpty falls, the entropy level increases. As he falls to the ground, the eggshells break and are scattered randomly. The substances inside the shells—the egg yolk and the albumen—are not mixed together, but remain as separate components. The increase in entropy causes the system to become less coherent, less ordered.
 The law of entropy says that a closed system will tend to go from a state of high order to a state of low order. If a system is not in equilibrium with its surroundings, it will dissipate energy and heat, and move toward equilibrium. This happens in all systems. Suns and stars, for example, are constantly dissipating energy and heating up. The law of entropy says that within a closed system, the total energy of the universe always remains constant.
 Another way to explain entropy is to consider a cup of coffee. A cup of coffee is a closed system; it is isolated from its surroundings. If the cup is left alone, the coffee will continue to cool. The entropy level of the coffee will increase as the coffee cools. However, if we add more heat to the coffee, the entropy level will decrease.
 The second law of thermodynamics is not a prediction or a general rule. It is not a statement about the future; it is a statement about the past. We can't undo entropy; once it has happened, it is irreversible. The cup of coffee will always cool and the coffee will always become more disordered.
 The second law of thermodynamics does not say that all things are limited to going from high order to low order, but rather that this is the most likely outcome. All systems tend toward equilibrium because they are constantly dissipating energy and losing order.
The second law of thermodynamics is also known as the law of increasing entropy.
Note : This law is sometimes called the law of increasing disorder. This name is misleading because the law applies to all change, not just disorder.

But he and his men reached Tripoli in February, where he rejoined the rest of the 1st Division. He was appointed commander of the 1st Brigade, which included the 22nd Battalion.
The 1st Brigade was put to use in a counter-attack on the German forces that had advanced to within 150 miles of Benghazi. The attack on Benghazi in April 1942 was launched four months after the German conquest of Tobruk. The Germans were supported by the Italian forces. The 1st Brigade was assigned to a position near Sidi Rezegh, 75 miles from Tobruk, and it was during this battle that Andrew was wounded.
Andrew was shot through the right shoulder. The bullet entered his shoulder and passed through his lungs. He was taken to a field hospital and then to a hospital in Cairo, where he was operated on. After being discharged from hospital, Andrew was sent to London for a second operation. During his time in hospital, he was visited by the Canadian prime minister, William Lyon Mackenzie King, who had come to England to meet the new British king, George VI, on his first visit to the United Kingdom. During the war years, King would visit Andrew frequently in hospital and would send him parcels of books to read.
The King was fascinated by Andrew's medical condition and was impressed by the fact that he was already reading and writing. He was also fascinated by the fact that Andrew was still serving. He asked him to write for him a story about the battles he was engaged in during the war. Andrew was also given a paralyzed arm and a wheelchair, but he insisted on using his own arm, which he disliked.
Andrew was still in London when the war ended in May 1945. He was not released from hospital until January 1946. He was then sent to a rehabilitation centre to recover his strength. He was appointed commander of the army's 4th Division in England. He was awarded the French Croix de Guerre and the Belgian Croix de Guerre.

In the absence of orders coordinating evacuation from the field ambulances , the Assistant Director of Medical Services ( ADMS

) sent a message to the medical officers stationed at the forward posts , requesting them to consolidate the corpses in their area and expedite the evacuation of the wounded. As the medical officers were too heavily engaged in treating the wounded to carry out this task , most of the evacuation was carried out by the Indian Army's ancillary corps such as the Corps of Engineers , the Pioneers , the Corps of Signals and the Military Police , all of whom were well versed in the technicalities of dealing with human remains .
The "canonical" method of dealing with human remains was to prepare them for cremation. Cremation was the only method of disposal officially sanctioned by the army. Back in June 1944, the Chief of the Imperial General Staff, Alanbrooke, had written to the Secretary of State for India, Sir Archibald Wavell, requesting that the burning of corpses be "discouraged" since it was a "bad precedent and a disgusting practice". In Wavell's view, "allowing the cremation of dead soldiers would not be politically acceptable in India". He added that "so far as is possible, we must see to it that the Indian people are not exposed to this sight".
Archbishop Frederic Daniel D'Souza of Lahore took the initiative in suggesting that the Christian graveyards be used for the burial of bodies. The ADMS and the Indian Army's Chaplain General, Colonel C. G. Armytage, agreed that this was feasible. However, they also recognised that in the event of a large number of dead, the graveyards would not be able to cope. In the event of a large number of casualties, the ADMS, with a view to preventing the "unpleasant" sight of cremation, suggested that it would be necessary to use large pits and to "bury the bodies, after proper preparation, in large trenches".
United Nations forces, including those of the USA and the UK , had the same experience as the Indian Army in dealing with the dead after the initial battles. The British War Office had issued a directive about the handling of corpses in battle. It stated that, in the event of a "major battle", there would be a large number of dead and the "great majority" would have to be "buried in the field". The directive added:
The task of burying the dead is, in the circumstances, one which must be undertaken by the troops themselves . . . The temporary burial of the dead in the field is a military necessity, and the men must be trained to carry out this work.
Although the directive was issued to the British Army, it was also distributed to the Commonwealth armies, including the Indian Army.
In the battle for Kohima , the British Indian Army was required to bury the dead in the field since the cemeteries were inadequate to cope with the casualties. After the battle, the 2nd Royal Leicestershire Regiment and the 1st Queen's Own Sappers and Miners were each responsible for the burial of the dead in their own battalion area. This would have been a difficult task even if there had been a sufficient number of men to do it. Unfortunately, the fighting continued for another seven days. "It was difficult to conceive of the magnitude of the task, which, in addition to the newly-fallen, had to include the burial of the many who had lain unburied in the fighting line for some days or indeed weeks," recalls the Director of Medical Services of the 2nd Royal Leicestershire Regiment, Lieutenant Colonel A. E. C. Broadbent.
The number of bodies buried in the field was not the same as the total number of casualties. The remainder of the dead were cremated by the military. The crematorium at the base of the 2nd Royal Leicestershire Regiment was "small and easily built" and "soon became known as 'The Furnace'". Colonel Broadbent recalls that the "cremation procedure was a simple one. The body was laid on a table in the furnace, and petrol lighted. It was then covered with a sheet of iron and the door closed by a padlock. The ashes were then collected and buried in a pit".
The cremation of corpses had been the subject of intense debate in India during the war. On 13 February 1945, the Viceroy stated that, in dealing with the dead, "we must take great care that no offence is given to the sensibilities of the people of India

the proposed route. A spokesman for the group stated that the citizens  committee had been set up to "better inform the public on the general course of the road" and to "dispel rumors and misinformation." He expressed the belief that the group "would be able to reach out to both sides of the issue and hopefully come to an agreement on the best route" for the toll road. The committee held more than 20 public meetings at which a traffic engineer and land use planners explained the route alternatives and responded to citizen questions. The committee was funded by $1,800 in contributions from the cities of Pearland and Friendswood.
A third group , the Citizens for Quality Growth , was formed in October 1982 by the communities of Friendswood, League City, and the Pearland Development Corporation to garner support for the toll road. The group's stated purpose was to "monitor the development of the proposed toll road" and to work to ensure that the toll road was developed in a manner that "will maintain the quality of life in these communities."
Another group , the Bay Area Toll Road Alliance , was formed in January 1983. This group was funded by the South Belt Citizens Committee, the Pearland Development Corporation, and the Friendswood Development Corporation. The alliance's stated purpose was "to keep the public informed of the progress of the Bay Area Toll Road."
A fourth group , the Galveston Bay Area Toll Road Alliance , was formed in January 1983. This group was made up of the Carverdale Homeowners Association, the Galveston Bay Area Toll Road Citizens Committee, and the Friendswood Development Corporation. The stated purpose of the alliance was "to monitor the development of the Bay Area Toll Road."
In September 1983, the Citizens for Quality Growth, the Galveston Bay Area Toll Road Alliance, and the Bay Area Toll Road Alliance merged to form the Bay Area Toll Road Alliance. This organization was still in existence at the time of the analysis.
The Bay Area Toll Road Alliance, in addition to its stated purpose of keeping the public informed of the progress of the Bay Area Toll Road, also sponsored a local referendum on the issue. The referendum was held in May of 1983, and voters were asked to decide whether they supported the proposed toll road. The referendum passed by a vote of 60% to 40%.
The Bay Area Toll Road Alliance also sponsored another referendum in May of 1985. This referendum was held in the communities of Friendswood, League City, and Pearland and was again asked to decide whether the community supported the proposed toll road. The referendum again passed by a vote of 60% to 40%.
In addition to these formal groups, the Bay Area Toll Road also had the support of several local politicians and officials. The League City Mayor and the Pearland City Council were both public supporters of the toll road. The League City Mayor was quoted as saying that League City "would benefit most of all from the toll road." The Pearland City Council expressed support for the toll road by agreeing to contribute up to $100,000 to help build it.

The Ottoman Empire also fought several battles in the Caucasus and in Mesopotamia (now Iraq and Kuwait).
After the collapse of the Ottoman Empire in 1922, the Ottoman Army was dissolved and the Turkish Army, the Turkish Air Force and the Turkish Navy were established in its place.

## Background

Lennon had conceived the idea for "Imagine" on the evening of 13 May 1971, while he was in the studio recording his album Imagine. In an interview with Rolling Stone published on 7 October 1980, Lennon recalled how he had been "feeling a bit depressed and a bit fed up and a bit nutty ... and I just started to think, 'Well, imagine there's no heaven, imagine there's no countries, imagine no religion, imagine no possessions'." He added: "I was trying to imagine a new world. Because there was so much war, so much chaos, so much confusion. And I just wrote it down, and I thought, 'Well, that's a nice idea.'"

Lennon's original recording of the song for his Imagine album was made in May 1971 at Ascot Sound Studios, on the first night of recording following his return from Los Angeles to England. This recording was Lennon's "original idea" for the song, with two verses that did not appear in the final version: "Imagine all the people living for today" and "Imagine there's no countries".

The recording was produced by Phil Spector, who was responsible for the orchestral arrangement of the song. The recording was made in mono, and Spector asked Lennon to sing the song again, with the volume turned up. Spector's assistant, Alan Klein, was present during the recording, and Lennon asked him to "put some cymbals in". A second, overdubbed version of the song was recorded with drums, two acoustic guitars, a piano, and Spector's orchestra. Lennon also sang the song with a higher vocal pitch than the original.

"Imagine" is a song of political and social commentary written in the key of A major in a 4/4 time signature. The song has a moderate tempo of 96 beats per minute.

The song's lyrics explore the opposite of what Lennon described as "the human race trading bits of paper for security". In the first verse, the singer imagines a world with no heaven. In the second verse, the singer considers a world with no countries, or possessions, or religion. The third verse imagines a world with no war, no hate, and no borders. Berg is a station on the Sognsvann Line ( line 6 ) of the Oslo Metro in Norway . Located between Ullevål stadion and Tåsen stat

io n, it is located in the district of Grorud .
The station was opened in 1935 and was only accessible by tram until 1989, when the Oslo Metro took over operations.
Berg is located at the end of the Sognsvann Line. The station is located next to the Moldeveien in Grorud.
The station is located in a residential area between Tåsen and Ullevål. Most of the passengers use this station to reach a nearby school, to the sports facilities in the neighboring Ullevål stadion and to the Grorud Valley shopping center.
Because of the nearby Ullevål stadion, which is used by the football club Vålerenga, Berg is also used by many football fans. The station is thus used by around 2,000 passengers per day, most of whom travel to Vålerenga.
In the late 1990s, the Oslo Tramway Company ( Oslo Sporveier ) planned to extend the Sognsvann Line to Skøyen as part of a new tramway ring line. After a referendum in 2001, the plan was dropped.
In 2012, the city council decided to renovate the station in the course of the upgrade of the Sognsvann Line. The city council would then invest 14 million kroner for the renovation of Berg and the station at Skarpsno. The upgrade of Berg was completed in 2014 .

The revolution also led to urbanization and the rise of the factory system.

On the other hand, the Turks were deeply engaged in their own front with the Russians, the Turcos being forced to fight on two fronts at once. The war in the Caucasus was at this time reaching its climax; and as the Russians were advancing and the Turcos were retreating, they could afford to send a few battalions of troops to occupy the Sinai.
The Turcos, who had hitherto operated from the desert, now moved into the Sinai itself, and established themselves in the neighbourhood of Rafa, on the western shore of the Gulf of Suez, and at El Arish and Wady Halfa on the eastern shore. The latter two positions were in the neighbourhood of, and fairly close to, the canal. The Turcos were still heavily engaged with the Russians, and were therefore far too weak to consider a serious offensive action against the British.
Sir Garnet Wolseley , who had been appointed Commander-in-Chief of the British forces in Egypt, had established his headquarters in the small town of Cairo, which was situated on the eastern shore of the Nile, some fifty miles from Alexandria, and about a hundred miles from Suez. On 1 July 1882 the British Admiral, Sir Beauchamp Seymour , was appointed to take charge of the blockade of the Red Sea. On 14 July 1882, Sir Beauchamp received from Sir Garnet Wolseley the following instructions for the operations of the British forces in Egypt:
(1) To blockade the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.
(2) To prevent the landing of any enemy force in the Sinai Peninsula.
(3) To compel the cessation of hostilities by the Turcos on the Canal.
(4) To prevent the departure of any Turkish fleet from Alexandria.
(5) To keep the enemy's fleet in the Red Sea and to prevent the Turcos from obtaining reinforcements from the Mediterranean.
(1) To bombard the forts at El Arish and Wady Halfa.
(2) To bombard the forts at Rafa.
(3) To obtain a foothold in the Sinai Peninsula by the occupation of El Arish.
(4) To occupy the canal, and to prevent the Turcos from using it.
(5) To prevent the Turcos from using the Suez Canal.
(6) To enable steamers to pass through the Suez Canal.
(7) To preserve the safety of the canal and the shipping on the Red Sea.
(8) To prevent the enemy from using the Suez Canal for the conveyance of troops.
(9) To prevent the enemy from using the Suez Canal for the conveyance of supplies.
(10) To occupy the canal, and to prevent the Turcos from using it.
(11) To carry out the instructions of the British Government as far as possible.
The command of the Egyptian coast and the Red Sea was divided between Sir Beauchamp Seymour , who was in command of the fleet, and the troops under Sir Garnet Wolseley . The latter were divided into two columns: (1) the Suez Column, under Sir Gerald Graham , and (2) the Eastern Column, under Sir Archibald Alison . The Suez Column was intended to operate against the forts on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Suez; the Eastern Column was intended to operate against the forts on the western shore of the gulf.
Sir Garnet's first step was to establish a naval blockade of the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, to prevent the Turcos from obtaining reinforcements, and to prevent the departure of any Turkish fleet from Alexandria. On 30 July 1882 the Turcos abandoned their position at Rafa and retired to El Arish. The Turcos also evacuated the forts at El Arish and Wady Halfa.

According to the Mortal Kombat: Deception character biography, he left the Lin Kuei after a failed coup d'état, and became obsessed with the thirst for revenge against them and the conquering of his homeland, Outworld. Sub-Zero's first appearance was in Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance, where he was hired by Shang Tsung to work as a mercenary during the tournament. He was introduced as a new character, in addition to his regular character, the blue-clad ninja Kuai Liang. The two characters were originally meant to be a single character, but the developers decided to have them separate for practicality.

### Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance

Sub-Zero is first seen after he is hired by Shang Tsung to participate in the Mortal Kombat tournament. He quickly defeats the first two opponents he encounters, Rain and Nightwolf. He faces off against Sonya Blade next, who was hired by Johnny Cage to protect the Earthrealm warriors. Sub-Zero manages to get the upper hand against Sonya, but she is able to defeat him by using her ice powers. Sub-Zero is also able to defeat the thunder god Raiden and the evil sorcerer Quan Chi. Sub-Zero later encounters Sonya again in the finals. After a brief battle, Sub-Zero manages to gain the upper-hand and is about to kill her, when a portal opens and Shinnok enters it, teleporting away with Sonya.

### Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks

Sub-Zero appears in Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks as a stage boss in the Outworld stage. In the game's storyline, he battles his brother, Bi-Han, also known as Noob Saibot. When Bi-Han defeats Sub-Zero, he retrieves his scepter and leaves without killing him. The scepter was then stolen by Shang Tsung, who used it to summon Shinnok.

### Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance and Mortal Kombat: Deception

Sub-Zero is defeated by Sonya Blade in the Mortal Kombat tournament. After the tournament, he is approached by Shang Tsung, who offers him a chance to get revenge by joining his service. Sub-Zero accepts Shang Tsung's offer and is later sent to infiltrate the Lin Kuei. While there, he discovers that the Lin Kuei has plans to conquer the Outworld. After Sub-Zero arrives in the Outworld, he is confronted by Bi-Han, who is also seeking revenge against the Lin Kuei, and the two become allies. Sub-Zero and Bi-Han join forces to destroy the Lin Kuei for good.

In Mortal Kombat: Deception, Sub-Zero and Bi-Han are also known as Noob Saibot and Smoke respectively. In addition to battling each other, they also battle the Lin Kuei's master, Shinnok, who has been resurrected and is seeking to conquer the Mortal Kombat universe. During the finals, Sonia Blade defeats Noob Saibot, and Bi-Han defeats Smoke, and both brothers are killed by Shinnok. Noob Saibot later appears as a boss in the Outworld stage.

Super Science Stories was an American pulp science fiction magazine published by Popular Publications from 1940 and 1943 , and

1950 and 1954. It was edited by Raymond A. Palmer who was also its editor for its 1950–54 revival.
Following the success of his editorship of Amazing Stories, Raymond A. Palmer became editor of Super Science Stories in 1940. He also had a regular column called "The Imaginative Man". He remained editor until the magazine was discontinued in 1943.
In 1950 Popular Publications revived Super Science Stories which ran until 1954 and was edited by Palmer until 1952. The magazine published one issue in 1955, and became a sister magazine to Amazing Stories.
The magazine published a total of 27 issues. As well as science fiction stories, the magazine also published articles on astronomy by Fred Whipple and on "the future of mankind" by John W. Campbell, Jr.

The label had originally planned to release the album in November 2002. However, Carey delayed the album's release to December 2002. During the recording process, Carey's personal and professional life were in turmoil. She separated from her husband, and her brother had been arrested on weapons charges. She was also recovering from a hip injury, which caused her to have to cancel a string of concerts in Japan.
Carey had an image change for the album; she had dyed her hair blonde, and she wanted to be known more for her songwriting than for her vocal abilities. She wrote the lyrics to the song " Can't Take That Away (Mariah's Theme)" , while her brother wrote the melody. Almost all of the songs were written with the assistance of production team the Matrix, who had worked with the Spice Girls . The album was originally titled Charmbracelet , but was subsequently renamed The Emancipation of Mimi.
Carey began recording the album in January 2002. The album is composed of 15 songs, and was produced by Carey, Jermaine Dupri and Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis. It features a variety of musical styles, including hip hop , R&B , soul , pop and ballads. The album features guest appearances from rappers Jay-Z , Big Sean , T.I. and " Weezy" of the Cash Money Millionaires , as well as singer Usher . The album's lyrics focus on Carey's personal life.
The album was set for release on November 19, 2002, but was delayed to December 10, 2002. The album debuted at number one on the US Billboard 200 with 463,000 copies sold in its first week. The album has been certified three times platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for shipments of three million copies. The album has sold seven million copies worldwide.
The album received mixed reviews from music critics. Critics praised the album's production and songwriting, but found the lyrics to be poor. The album spawned three singles; "Loverboy", "We Belong Together" and "Shake It Off". " We Belong Together " topped the US Billboard Hot 100 for eleven weeks. The album was nominated for two Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year.

The Diwan has notified the hotel owner, Dhanna (Nana Palsikar), about the booking, although he tells the Diwan that he "has a better idea". Dhanna's son, Sunder (Amitabh Bachchan), has been away from home for the past few months, and he has come back "to marry a rich girl". A comedy of errors and misunderstandings ensue when Raja and Radha find out that they are mistakenly sharing a room with an unmarried man, and that Dhanna is trying to marry off his son to a rich family.

## Biography

General Saprang Kalayanamitr was born on August 27, 1979 in Thailand .

## Career

General Saprang Kalayanamitr made her acting debut in 2003 as a supporting actress in the television series "Nang Sao Thai Noi" . She gained national fame after starring as Chaiyod in the 2006 television series "Dark Blue Kiss" . General Saprang Kalayanamitr also featured in the television series "Love of Siam" (2007), "Suffering Love" (2008), "Contemporary X Luang" (2009), "Love's Destiny" (2010) and "Heart of the Hero" (2011).

## Personal life

General Saprang Kalayanamitr married her college sweetheart, Doe-Thai actor Phonthip Panissara (Thai : พอนทิพย์ พานิสรา) in 2005, but the two divorced in 2008. In 2013, General Saprang Kalayanamitr married her longtime friend, Phra Somchai (Thai : พระสมชัย) , a member of the royal family .

Following the 2008 closing of Copia , a group of investors , developers , advocates , and vintners named the Coalition to Prese

ve Copia formed to re-open and re-purpose the complex. The group was chaired by BottleRock Napa Valley founder Dave Graham , and included Napa Valley Vintners Association members Don Schultz, Charles Swig, Don and Darcie Harris, and investor Kendall-Jackson Wine Estate & Winery founder Jess Jackson .

In 2013, the group began meeting with California State Parks and the Napa County Board of Supervisors to discuss the future of the site. The group approached the California State Parks to explore options to preserve the building, and lease the site for a private entity to rehabilitate and operate as a cultural center, with a focus on food, wine, and the arts. The park's proposal to demolish the building was met with strong opposition from the community, the Napa Valley Vintners Association, and the Napa County Board of Supervisors.

The Coalition to Preserve Copia proposed to lease and rehabilitate the site, including the Copia building, and operate it as a private entity. The Coalition to Preserve Copia submitted a bid to the State of California in June 2013. In February 2014, the California State Parks Department determined that the bid was not responsive to the Request for Proposals, and that the Coalition to Preserve Copia had failed to submit a timely response to the Request for Proposals.

In 2015, the Coalition to Preserve Copia submitted a new proposal to the State of California, with a focus on business and tourism development and conservation. The Coalition to Preserve Copia proposed leasing the site for a minimum of 25 years and providing $1.4 million in upfront capital. The Coalition to Preserve Copia also proposed a $1.6 million contribution to the Napa County Parks Foundation, which provides funding for California State Parks. The project was endorsed by Napa County Supervisor Bill Dodd , the Napa County Board of Supervisors, the Napa Valley Vintners Association, the Napa Valley Register , the Association of California Parks, and the Napa Valley Tourism Board.

The Coalition to Preserve Copia's proposal was rejected by California State Parks in February 2015.

In the following months, the Coalition to Preserve Copia engaged in discussions with the Napa County Board of Supervisors, the Napa Valley Vintners Association, and the Napa Valley Tourism Board. The Napa County Board of Supervisors unanimously approved a resolution endorsing the project. The Napa Valley Vintners Association endorsed the project. The Napa Valley Tourism Board endorsed the project, and appointed a representative to the Coalition to Preserve Copia.

The Napa Valley Wine Tasting Association is a nonprofit organization that promotes the wine and culinary arts in the Napa Valley. The Napa Valley Wine Tasting Association was established in 1934 to promote wine and culinary arts in the Napa Valley. The Napa Valley Wine Tasting Association has hosted wine tastings at the Copia building for over 30 years.

The corn crake 's breeding habitat is grassland , particularly hayfields , and it uses similar environments on the wintering gr

ound . It is found in southern and central Europe , western Asia , and North Africa . It has been introduced to England and Ireland .

Adult corn crake

## Taxonomy

The corn crake was first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1758. The scientific name of the corn crake is derived from Greek words meaning "corn" (kornos) and "crake" (poros).

## Description

The corn crake is 19 to 20 cm (7.5 to 7.9 in) long. Adults have a grey-brown back, wings and tail, with a white belly and breast. The eyes are dark brown, the bill is black and the legs are red. Juveniles are paler, with a pale brown back, wings and tail, and a yellow belly. The corn crake is often mistaken for the long-tailed crakes, which have longer tails and longer legs.

The corn crake is monogamous and breeds in loose colonies in habitat margins. The female lays 4–8 eggs in a ground scrape lined with grass and leaves. The chicks hatch after 18–21 days and are able to fly at 22–24 days. The corn crake is a migratory bird that winters in Africa.

## Habitat

The corn crake lives in open country with tall vegetation: moorland , heathland , pastures, agricultural fields, and lawns. It is often found in areas containing cereal crops, such as wheat , barley , and rye. It is not found in forests.

## Food and feeding

The corn crake feeds on seeds, small invertebrates and larvae.

## Predators

Some of the corn crake's predators include foxes , stoats (Mustela erminea) and weasels (Mustela nivalis).

## Migration

The corn crake is a migratory bird. It migrates from Great Britain and Ireland to Africa during the winter.

## Reproduction

The corn crake is a monogamous bird. It breeds in loose colonies of a few pairs. Pairs defend a territory of 0.5 to 1.0 hectares (1.2 to 2.5 acres). This territory is used by both the male and female to attract mates and defend against intruders. The male performs the majority of the courtship displays for the female. It bows, trembles, and makes a rattling noise. The male can also sing, which it does throughout most of the year. The song is a short, harsh call, which is repeated. During courtship, the male may also perform the "parachute display" by jumping up several feet in the air.

The female lays 4 to 8 eggs in a scrape in the ground lined with grass and leaves. The eggs are pale blue with brown spots. The female incubates the eggs. The chicks hatch after 18 to 21 days. Both parents feed the chicks. The chicks are able to fly at 22 to 24 days. The corn crake does not feed the chicks in the winter.

## Conservation

The corn crake is a common bird in the United Kingdom, although it has decreased in recent years. It is a red-listed bird in Ireland. It is extinct in the Netherlands and in Belgium it is critically endangered. It is extinct in Denmark and in France. In Germany, it is endangered.

The first factor in the decline of the kakapo was the arrival of humans . Māori folklore suggests that the kakapo was found thr

ashing about on the beach by a chief who was named Ariki-i-te-rangi. The chief allowed the bird to live in his canoe, but its weight caused it to overturn. In his anger he tried to cut off the bird's head, but his knife blade could not pierce the thick skin. When he raised his arm high, the kakapo spread its wings in a gesture of surrender and the chief decided to leave it alone. He released it and it flew off into the forest.
 Māori had been settling in New Zealand for several centuries when the first Europeans arrived in the late eighteenth century. At the time of the arrival of the first Europeans, Māori were already living in a society that was relatively stable, with the basic institutions of traditional society in place. It is likely that Māori were already familiar with the kakapo, as it was a well-known bird, and had most probably been hunted.
There is no evidence that the kakapo was eaten by Māori, but it was hunted for its skins and its significance as a taonga (treasure). It was also known as a source of food for dogs, which would be released to chase the kakapo into a tree where the dog could catch it.
The early European settlers also hunted the kakapo for its skins, which were used for waterproofing sails. Its eggs were collected by settlers, and to this day are still collected from the wild. In the early days of the colony the kakapo was killed by settlers in large numbers, and the birds were hunted for food. Its eggs and young were also eaten.
 The kakapo was not a species that was particularly sought after by hunters and was not actively hunted. It was not until the 1920s that the kakapo was recognised as an endangered species and hunting of the bird became more formalised.
 The introduction of firearms to New Zealand in the nineteenth century allowed for a better hunting experience for the settlers. The first recorded kill of a kakapo by a settler occurred in 1849.
The kakapo was still hunted by Māori up until the late 1800s.
 In 1900, kakapo were still being hunted. In 1908, a kakapo was shot by a settler named Mr.Miller on the island of Raoul. The bird was brought to the mainland and a reward of £200 was offered by the government for the return of the kakapo to its island, but the bird died before it could be returned.
The last known Māori kill of a kakapo was reported in 1914.
 By 1914, there were only 100 kakapo left in the world.
 After 1914, the hunting of kakapo became more organised. In 1916, the first hunting season was organised by the government, and a total of 90 birds were killed. This season was a great success for the hunters and a further 90 birds were killed in the 1917 season.
In 1918, the hunting of kakapo was banned.
 In 1919, the first kakapo was brought to the mainland and was taken to the Auckland Zoo.
 In 1922, the last kakapo in the world was killed in Fiordland.

Ceratopsia was coined by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1890 to include dinosaurs possessing certain characteristic features , includ

in horns, frills, and beaks . Marsh's cladistic definition of Ceratopsia is based on a series of shared characters, including a single row of horns on the nose, a parrot-like beak filled with small teeth, and a frill made of ossified skin extending from the back of the skull to the neck. These features are shared by most ceratopsids, but not all. The most obvious feature of ceratopsids is the beak-like snout, which distinguishes the group from other theropods with horns. The beak ended in a variety of horns, frills, and other projections. The earliest known genus, Psittacosaurus, had a beak and parrot-like teeth, but lacked a frill.
In the traditional view of ceratopsian taxonomy, Ceratopsia was regarded as a natural group consisting of all animals that shared the characters of a beak and a horn, regardless of their other anatomical similarities or differences. As a result, the group was divided into more or less arbitrarily defined subgroups, such as the Chasmosaurinae, Centrosaurinae, and Ceratopsidae. However, the concept of a natural group was never formally defined, and was gradually abandoned in the 1990s in favor of a cladistic view of taxonomy.
According to this system, Ceratopsia is a monophyletic group consisting of all animals that are more closely related to each other than to any other group. This concept is based on the phylogenetic tree, which shows the relationships of all animals based on their anatomical similarities and differences. In the tree, all members of a monophyletic group share a common ancestor, and all descendants of that ancestor form a monophyletic group. The ancestor of ceratopsids is known as Ceratopsia incertae sedis, or "Ceratopsia of uncertain position". The term "ceratopsian" is still used to refer to the group of animals that share a common ancestor with Ceratopsia, but the term does not refer to any specific group of animals.

Pokiri was shot predominantly in and around Hyderabad , especially in the Annapurna Studios , the aluminium factory near Gachib

owli , and the Nizamabad area, where the forest scenes were filmed. During filming, a set was created to resemble the Himalayas, consisting of a 40-foot-high (12 m) artificial mountain, with a 16-foot-high (5 m) artificial cave inside.
Pokiri was released theatrically on 30 September 2006 and was distributed by Wide Angle Creations, which is a wholly owned subsidiary of Sarigamaa Productions . The film was dubbed into Hindi and released on 24 November 2006, under the title Kick.
As of 24 November 2006, Pokiri has collected ₹ 22.75 crore (US$3.5 million) from the sale of tickets. The film grossed a total of ₹ 112 crore (US$18 million) worldwide, and its distributor, Wide Angle Creations, made a profit of ₹ 55 crore (US$8.3 million).
The film was initially titled " Rowdy " but was later changed to Pokiri, which means " thunder". The film was widely reported to be inspired by the films Dabangg and Kamal Haasan's 1987 film Ram Lakhan , but Bharath admits to being inspired by the 2004 film Love Story 2050 starring Harman Baweja and Priyanka Chopra.
Thaman S. scored the film's music. His songs " Kiss Kiss " became a rage among the youth, and the song " Swagatham " was also widely received. The songs were often played in dance clubs.
Kick was released on 24 November 2006. Upon release, the film received favourable reviews and performed well at the box office. Writing for Indiaglitz.com, Sangeetha Devi Dundoo wrote that "the film has all the elements of a commercial entertainer that keeps the audience glued to the screen".
