From there , Wheeler was invited to direct a Society of Antiquaries excavation at the Roman settlement of Verulamium , which ex

erted a lasting influence on his life.

In 1861, 22-year-old Wheeler joined the British School at Athens , where he studied under the famous classical archaeologist John L. Myres. His mentor provided Wheeler with a sound classical education in the context of British archaeology. Myres' work on the Mycenaean pottery industry exposed Wheeler to the use of palaeography in archaeology. In 1862, Wheeler was promoted to assistant secretary of the School, and he continued in this role for 25 years.

Wheeler's first excavation took place in 1864 in the ancient city of Baalbeck in Syria . Wheeler worked at Baalbek for three years, and he began to develop his methodology by comparing the historical record with the archaeological evidence, and in particular by considering the stratigraphy of the site.

In 1865, Wheeler was appointed to a professorship at the School of Archaeology, Art, and Architecture at the University of Berne , Switzerland . He held this position until 1867.

In 1868, Wheeler was appointed to the School of Archaeology at the University of Athens . He worked at the School until 1872, and then again from 1875 to 1876.

In 1879, Wheeler arrived at the site of Carchemish in Turkey on behalf of the British Museum, with a team of 100 workers.

In 1884, Wheeler founded the Museum of the Ancient Near East in London, which he ran until 1897.

In 1886, Wheeler was appointed to a professorship at the University of Pennsylvania , where he spent the remainder of his life. In 1888, Wheeler became the first director of the University Museum in Philadelphia, and he held this position until his retirement in 1906.

Wheeler was also a founding member of the American School of Oriental Research in Jerusalem .

Wheeler was elected as a Fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London in 1888, and as a Fellow of the British Academy in 1908.

## Work

### Carchemish

Wheeler excavated extensively at Carchemish, where he discovered tablets in the Assyrian language. He also discovered the city's necropolis, which contained thousands of burials, and he reconstructed the city's plan from the distribution of these burials.

Wheeler's tablets from Carchemish were later used by Sir Henry Rawlinson, and would prove crucial in deciphering the cuneiform script.

### Philadelphia

Wheeler produced many volumes on the archaeology of the Middle East. In Philadelphia, Wheeler was responsible for the creation of the University Museum, which was made up of four separate museums: the Girard Exhibit, the Egyptian Exhibit, the Museum of the Ancient Near East, and the University Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology.

Wheeler was responsible for over 900 publications on archaeology, including "Egyptian Archaeology: A Topical Outline" (1905) and "The Excavations at Carchemish" (1904).

### Israel

Wheeler's work in Israel included the excavation of Tell Qasile, Tell Kafrit, and Tel Megiddo .

Wheeler's "Geography and Ceramics of Palestine" (1896) contains some of his earliest research into the pottery of Palestine. From the pottery found at Megiddo, Wheeler was able to identify the date of the Egyptian occupation of the city to the 14th century BC, and he also identified a connection between the pottery found at Megiddo and Tell Qasile.

### Other work

Wheeler carried out excavations at Crete, and he was also responsible for the reconstruction of the Minoan palaces at Knossos and Phaistos.

Wheeler's work also included the excavation of the ruins of the ancient city of Mycenae on the Peloponnese.

### Museums

Wheeler left a legacy of museums in North America and Europe.

The similarities between A. chailletii and A. areolatum have caused some confusion regarding their placement in the genus . As

the genus was circumscribed in 1980, the dorsal surface of A. chailletii lacks the distinctive areolate markings characteristic of A. areolatum. Furthermore, the pistillum of A. chailletii is distinctive and, unlike those of other A. species, is not enclosed within a hinged operculum.
 A. chailletii was first described as a species by Stapf and Leighton in 1895. As no type material has been found, the description is a lectotype. The lectotype specimen was previously attributed to A. areolatum but was subsequently identified as A. chailletii.
The species was again described by Van der Hoeven in 1980 as a subspecies of A. areolatum. The lectotype of A. areolatum is a specimen collected by Stapf and Leighton. The lectotype specimen of A. chailletii  was collected by Van der Hoeven. A. chailletii was subsequently described as a species by Van der Hoeven in 1984.
 The species epithet chailletii is derived from the family name of Denis Chaillet (1927–2002), a Canadian orchid enthusiast.
A. areolatum  (Gagnep.) S.C.Chen & J.J.Wood was described as a species by S. C. Chen and John Jeffrey Wood in 1990.
 A. areolatum was first described as a species by Gagnepain in 1942. The type specimen was collected by Gagnepain in Yunnan Province, China and is housed at the Herbier National de Paris.
The species epithet areolatum is derived from the Latin word areola, meaning "little island".
 A. areolatum was subsequently described as a subspecies of A. chailletii by Van der Hoeven in 1980.

The Importance of Being Earnest was one of Wilde's most successful plays, though it was not well received by the critics. In a special issue of The Nineteenth Century and After, the leading monthly journal of literature, it was referred to as a "bubble of froth", and Wilde himself was said to have been "too much of a dandy to be a serious artist".
The first performance had been on 14 February 1895, but Wilde was not arrested until 5 April. He was tried on 25 May 1895, and was found guilty of gross indecency. He was sentenced to two years of hard labour. During this period, Wilde wrote De Profundis, a long letter which was published in 1905. After his release from prison, he left immediately for France, where he died destitute in a Paris hotel room at the age of 46.
Wilde has been the subject of numerous plays and films portraying his relationship with Bosie.
Oscar Fingal O'Flahertie Wills Wilde (16 October 1854 – 30 November 1900) was an Irish playwright and poet. After writing in different forms throughout the 1880s, he became one of London's most popular playwrights in the early 1890s. He is remembered for his epigrams, his novel The Picture of Dorian Gray, his plays, as well as the circumstances of his imprisonment and early death.
The Importance of Being Earnest is a play by Oscar Wilde. It is a farcical comedy in which the protagonists maintain fictitious personae to escape burdensome social obligations. Working within the social conventions of late Victorian London, the play's major themes are the triviality with which it treats institutions as serious as marriage, and the resulting lack of responsibility with which these institutions are treated.
The Importance of Being Earnest is Wilde's most popular play.

The Importance of Being Earnest is one of Oscar Wilde's most popular plays, and it is often performed. However, its popularity has meant it has been translated into many languages , though the homophonous puns and many of the wordplay make successful translation problematic.
In the English-speaking world, the play has been translated into American English by Howard E. Rollins, Jr. (1982), and into Australian English by Peter Hicks. In the non-English-speaking world, the play has been translated into French by Jacques Ancelot, and into Spanish by Luis de Peralta.
The play has been translated into Finnish by Pertti Lassila (1996), German by Oskar Drott, and Greek by Dimitris Katsikopoulos. The play has also been adapted into Russian by Nikolai Chernyshevski.
The play was adapted for television in a 1952 production directed by Marcel Varnel, but it has not been adapted for film.

The Jurchens were a Tungusic @-@ speaking group of semi @-@ agrarian tribes inhabiting areas of northeast Asia that are now par

celled between Russia, China, and North Korea, where they formed the basis of the Koryo dynasty. They were probably related to the Manchu, as well as to the Mongols and the Turks. They were expert archers, riding on horseback, and they were good hunters.
The Jurchen were the first of the nomadic peoples to challenge the power of the Khitans. They were led by Aguda, whose grandfather, Kusul, had converted to Buddhism, changed his name to Alaqai, and united the Jurchens. Aguda had a son named Wuzhu, who was crowned emperor in 1161.
In 1161, the Jurchen defeated the Kitan Liao dynasty, and with the help of the Song dynasty, they entered Beijing and established the Jin dynasty (1115–1234) in China. They also took control of the Khitan capital of Zhongdu (today's Beijing). The Jurchens were not originally Buddhists, but the Kitan priest Jingjue (1107–1173) managed to convince the Jurchen emperor Wuzhu to follow the teachings of the Buddha.
As the Jurchens were predominantly steppe people, they were in conflict with the Han Chinese, who had been gradually pushed to the south by the Mongols and Turkic steppe peoples. The Jurchens were the first steppe people to conquer and rule northern China. They were able to do so by the help of the Song dynasty, which was too weak to stop them.
The Jurchen were the first of the Northeast Asian steppe peoples to conquer the south, and in 1127, they took control of the Song dynasty capital of Lin'an (today's Hangzhou). In 1126, Emperor Huizong of the Song dynasty was captured while fleeing to the south with his court. He died in captivity. In 1130, the Song emperor Gaozong (1107–1187) was also captured and died in captivity.
In 1127, the Jurchen emperor Wuzhu moved the capital from Zhongdu to Kaifeng (today's Kaifeng in Henan province), where he changed the name of the country to Jin. He also changed the Chinese name of his dynasty to Da-Jin, or Great Jin.
The Jurchens were also known as the Jurchen-Kitan, or Jin (Tungusic) or Jin (Manchu). Their name for themselves was Jurchen-Jin.
The Khitan founded the Liao dynasty in 907, and ruled much of today's northern China and northern Korea. The Jurchens destroyed the Liao dynasty in 1125, and established the Jin dynasty. The descendants of the Khitan migrated to Yuanmingyuan (known as the "Garden of Perfect Brightness" or "Summer Palace"), which is now part of Beijing.
The Song dynasty was a cultural and commercial center for Asia. It was the most populous and prosperous of the Chinese dynasties, with about 100 million people, and a large merchant class, most of whom were Buddhists.
The Song dynasty was known for its advances in mathematics, medicine, literature, and the arts. The literature of the Song dynasty, called the classical Chinese novel, was highly developed. It was also known for its scientific advances in medicine and metallurgy.

After the Franks were driven from the Holy Land in 1291 , European familiarity with the castles of the Crusades declined . It w

as not until the 1790 s that the castles of the Crusades again became a subject of popular interest. The two most important travel books of the period are the _Travels in the Middle Ages_ (1792) by the English canon Edward Gibbon and the _Travels through Southern Italy_ (1800) by the English vicar William Wood. Both books cover the Crusader castles of Europe.
In the _Travels_ , Gibbon describes the Crusader castles of the Holy Land, which he had seen in 1759 on his way to Rome. He is particularly interested in the castles of the Crusaders in the Middle Ages. Castles are mentioned in almost every chapter, and Gibbon often comments on the apparent accidental similarity of the Crusader castles of western Europe and the Middle East.
In 1790 Gibbon travelled to Rome, and in the following year he published his _Travels in the Middle Ages._ Chapter 29 deals with the Crusader castles of the Holy Land. After describing the castles of Acre, Gibbon also writes about the castles of the Holy Land in the Middle Ages.
In 1798 Gibbon published the first four volumes of his _History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire_. The fifth and last volume was published in 1814. Gibbon wrote the _Decline and Fall_ during the years 1776–88. In the first part of the book (which was published in 1788), Gibbon devotes a chapter to the Crusades. After having described them in his _Travels_ , Gibbon now describes the Crusader castles of Europe.
The _Travels_ and the _History_ both deal with the Crusader castles of the Middle Ages. The _History_ is obviously more detailed than the _Travels_. In the _History_ , the Crusader castles of the Holy Land are only briefly mentioned (pp. 546–8, 550–2, 555–6, 573–5, 578–9, 585–6, 648–50, 653–5, 680–3). In the _Travels_ , the Crusader castles of the Holy Land are discussed in detail. Gibbon also discusses the Crusader castles of the Middle Ages in Europe.
In 1798, the year in which Gibbon published the first four volumes of his _History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire_ , the travel writer William Wood published his _Travels through Southern Italy_ , which is also devoted to the Crusader castles. Wood's book is not as well known as Gibbon's, but the two books are often compared.
William Wood was an English vicar. In 1792 he went to Italy on a trip that lasted ten months. In 1797 he published his travel memoirs.
Wood's book is written in the form of a journal. He describes his travels in the form of letters to his friend and patron Sir William Hamilton. The letters are addressed to 'My dear Sir William'. In the introduction to the first volume Wood explains his system of using letters.
There are 26 letters. The letters are not, however, numbered – even though this would have been the obvious system. Wood's _Travels_ is a journal in which the author discusses his thoughts, not only his experiences.
In the introduction to the second volume, Wood writes that he has had to leave out much from his _Travels_ and that he has also 'omitted many details, designed to amuse and delight'.
Wood's book is therefore not only a travel book, but also a journal and a diary. It is a description of travels and a report of the author's daily experiences, but it is not as systematic as a diary.
Wood's travels in southern Italy began in 1792. In the first chapter of the book, he describes how he arrived in Naples on 17 September. His journey from England to Naples lasted fourteen weeks, and he arrived in Naples on 17 September. It is not clear exactly when Wood published his book. The 25th Infantry Division (US) was reconstituted in Hawaii, United States in 1967 as a reserve formation of the United States Army . It was activated on 1 October 2015 .

The first permanent unit raised was the 1 st Military District or 1 st Military Area, which comprised the South Australian Mounted Infantry and the South Australian Garrison Artillery. The 1 st SA Garrison Artillery was formed in June 1903 from the South Australian Garrison Artillery and the South Australian Volunteer Artillery. It was composed of one battery of four guns in Adelaide , one battery of four guns in Port Adelaide, and one battery of four guns in Alice Springs. The 1 st SA Garrison Artillery was disbanded in 1912, with the headquarters at Adelaide moving to Gawler. In 1913 the 1 st Gawler Garrison Artillery was formed. The 2 nd SA Garrison Artillery, another four-gun battery, was raised at Adelaide in 1903. It was disbanded in 1907. In 1903 the 1 st South Australian Mounted Infantry was formed from the South Australian Mounted Rifles. It was disbanded in 1908, but at the end of 1912 it was re-raised, this time as the 1 st South Australian Mounted Rifles, a unit with a strength of 218 men. The 2 nd SA Mounted Infantry was formed in February 1904 from the South Australian Mounted Rifles, and it was disbanded in 1909. In 1912 it was re-formed as the 1 st South Australian Mounted Rifles. All these units were part-time soldiers, who were called out for training in April and September each year, and for active service in the event of war.
As a result of the threat of war with Germany, the Commonwealth Military Forces were reorganised. The 1 st Military District was divided into two areas of operations, the 1 st Military Area and the 2 nd Military Area. The 1 st Military Area was based in Adelaide , and it comprised the 1 st SA Mounted Rifles and the 1 st SA Garrison Artillery. The 2 nd Military Area was based in Port Adelaide, and it comprised the 1 st SA Mounted Rifles, the 1 st SA Garrison Artillery, and the 2 nd SA Garrison Artillery. As a method of birth control , male condoms have the advantages of being inexpensive , easy to use , having few side effects ,

and not requiring medical prescription .  According to the Center for Disease Control ,  the effectiveness of male condoms is 15 to 20%.  The most frequent reported side effects of condoms are their breakage , slippage , and interrupting during intercourse.
Condoms are made of various materials—latex , polyurethane , polyisoprene , and lamb or natural animal membranes. Latex is the most commonly used material. Lamb and natural animal membranes were used until the mid-20th century.  The latex condom became the standard for contraception in the 1970s.  Natural animal membranes are regarded as less safe than latex condoms.  Condoms are also made of polyurethane, which is recommended for people with latex allergies.

A rubber condom is a sheath-shaped device made of rubber or plastic, which is used during sexual intercourse to reduce the probability of pregnancy and spread of sexually transmitted diseases.
The word "condom" is derived from the name of the English town of Condom in the Gers department of France. In the 18th and 19th centuries, English travelers, having heard of a product made from the intestinal membranes of sheep and lambs, called it "Condom" in reference to the town.
The condom was invented in the 17th century by a physician in the Netherlands, known as the "Father of Latex", and was called a "rubber" for its elasticity.
The use of condoms as a method of birth control is first mentioned in Babylonian inscriptions from the 2nd millennium BC. They were made of animal intestines and were introduced into Europe by the Egyptians. The Romans used them to prevent pregnancy and disease. The condom was used as a contraceptive in the 18th and 19th centuries.

NTSB investigators concluded that the likely cause of the crash was pilot error . The board concluded that Clay and Polehinke i

ed to avoid a storm, and that the crew had been misled on the radio by air traffic control.
When Clay's plane crashed, he did not eject. There were no survivors.
The NTSB does not believe Clay and Polehinke intended to crash the plane . But the agency's investigators concluded that they did die a few miles away from the airport, when they could have landed safely.
The report said: "The pilots were at a point in the flight where, with proper instrument flying skills, they could have successfully returned to the airport. But they were unfamiliar with the instrument approach procedure and became disoriented.
"The NTSB believes that the pilots encountered airframe icing and the aircraft probably became airborne again. The airplane was probably flying in circles for a period of time.
"The pilots probably became disoriented and the airplane flew into the ground."
The investigators concluded that Clay and Polehinke were not intoxicated. They said there was no evidence that either of them had been on drugs.
A cousin of Clay's, who was also a pilot, said Clay "was a very good pilot and I didn't want to believe he did anything wrong. But I've talked to several experienced pilots and they agreed that he must have done something wrong."
The NTSB board investigators found that Clay and Polehinke were "not familiar with the instrument approach procedures for the airport and became disoriented."
Several of Clay's friends said he had told them that he intended to fly to the airport. "He said he was going to fly the airplane to the airport, land it and sleep, and then go to work the next day."
The friends said he had never told them he intended to fly to Bismarck and then sleep in the plane and fly back to the Twin Cities the next day.
A week before the crash, Clay had been involved in two serious plane crashes.
On March 21, 1985, Clay was flying a Beech A100 from Indianapolis to the Twin Cities. When he was about 30 miles west of Minneapolis, he lost control, and the plane went into a dive, crashing into a field.
A few days later, Clay was flying a Beech A100 from Milwaukee to Indianapolis. During this flight, the plane ran out of fuel, and Clay had to put the plane down in a cornfield.
"I'm a little more cautious now than I used to be," Clay said. "I used to fly out in the middle of the night and do a lot of things I wouldn't do now."
"I have a lot of good things to say about John," said a friend. "He invited me to fly with him. I'd never flown before, and I was a little nervous. He handled the airplane so nice, and he was so patient with me. I felt like I was in good hands. I flew with him several times, and I enjoyed it. I don't think he ever had an accident."

Working out the average age of the GA fleet is difficult as there is no official record of all aircraft ever registered in the UK. This is because , in the absence of an official register , the Civil Aviation Authority (CAA ) relies on the manufacturer to register the aircraft in their name and then to register the aircraft with the CAA .
In addition , as a result of the 1995 Air Navigation Order , aircraft which have not been operated within the UK for more than 12 months may be deregistered . However , many aircraft are deregistered for a shorter period of time , and it is also possible to deregister the aircraft without transferring the ownership of the aircraft to the CAA . Indeed , most aircraft are deregistered as soon as they are sold , and this is the case even for aircraft which have been registered in the UK for many years.
However , the age of the UK GA fleet is not difficult to establish , provided that one assumes that all aircraft which are deregistered are scrapped for parts , and that aircraft which are deregistered and not scrapped are still in service .

W. H. Carre's School

W. H. Carre's School is a former private school, listed at grade II, in Wimbledon, London.

## History

The property dates from c.1842 and was built for the Rev. William Henry Carre, sometime of Trinity College, Cambridge. Carre (1819–1899) was a mathematics master at the University of Cambridge from 1845 to 1866, as well as a fellow there. He was also a Fellow of Trinity College and a schoolmaster there and at Wimbledon. 

Carre's maintained roughly 20 pupils on roll throughout the 1840s , but by 1858 , this had fallen to two free scholars and two paying scholars.

During the First World War, the school was requisitioned as the 'Village House for the Use of the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps' and housed a number of female soldiers.

## Architecture

The school is a two-storey stuccoed building with a central, octagonal, projecting bay. It is set within a large garden and is surrounded by a high brick wall.

Gasterosteus aculeatus is a generalist omnivore , eating detritus , algae , and fish . Other small animals may be eaten as well.
This species spawns from April to July , and may spawn more than once in a season. The eggs are laid in sandy areas near the shore , and are guarded by the male during development. The eggs, about 1 mm in diameter, hatch in 10 to 11 days. The young are free swimming at hatching. They grow at least 2 cm per year in length.
Gasterosteus aculeatus is the most widely distributed species of fish in the world .

During a tumultuous pioneer period characterized by its centrality in proximity to the Western United States , transportation i

s a ubiquitous theme. But within the context of the history of Utah, transportation has a special significance which is unique.
The pioneers, who were mostly Mormon converts, found themselves in a new land, without most of their material possessions, and in a terrain that was not only hostile to the newcomers, but which was unfamiliar to them.
The pioneers were used to the comforts of civilization, the amenities of city life, and the conveniences of the modern age, none of which were easily adaptable to the new environment. The pioneers were, therefore, forced to improvise, to adapt, and to adjust themselves to the new environment.
Among the most important of these adaptations was transportation. Transportation became a vital necessity, and the pioneers had to find a way to transport themselves, their goods, their animals, and their supplies.
Their means of transportation were limited, and they were forced to rely largely on their own ingenuity and ingenuousness to overcome the obstacles that lay in their path.
There were few roads in Utah during the early pioneer period. Most of the roads were, however, in a wretched condition. The pioneers had to construct roads of their own, and in most cases they had to cut the roads through the wilderness.
The pioneers were accustomed to the luxury and convenience of railroads, and their first attempt at constructing a railroad was the ill-fated 1869 Harriman railroad from Salt Lake City to the Pacific Ocean.
The Harriman railroad was to follow the old Spanish trail, and the pioneers were to have a railroad that would take them from Salt Lake City to the West Coast, thereby relieving them of the long, arduous trip by wagon.
The Harriman railroad would have had a definite impact on the history of Utah and the West, but it failed. It failed because the pioneers, who had been accustomed to the luxury and convenience of railroads, would not make the sacrifice required to build a railroad. They were unwilling to abandon the comforts of civilization.
The failure of the Harriman railroad is one example of the pioneers' unwillingness to sacrifice. By not building the railroad, the pioneers were forced to improvise and to adapt as they made their way to the West.

Liverpool controlled the opening passages of the game . Their first goalscoring chance came in the 11th minute when Alan Kenned

ys free kick from the left struck the left-hand post. A minute later, Jimmy Melia missed a sitter from close range and, as the game wore on, the visitors defence would be unlucky not to concede a penalty when a foul on Stephen Crainey appeared to warrant a spot-kick.
Liverpool were now in control, but a crucial mistake by Jamie Carragher enabled the visitors to take the lead. A long ball from the halfway line to Danny Cadamarteri was poorly judged by the Liverpool defender, and the ball dropped to the feet of the substitute striker, who was unmarked in the area. He looked up and, with an unerring shot, he beat James in the Liverpool goal to give Rovers the lead.
Within the first half, however, Gerrards equaliser was on the cards, and the midfielder made no mistake with the chance. Carragher headed the ball towards Gerrard, who had raced on to the ball, and the redshirt leader controlled the ball and shot low past Brad Friedel to draw Liverpool level.
Half-time brought a double substitution, with Danny Murphy and Harry Kewell replacing Sami Hyypia and Steve Finnan respectively.
Kewell immediately made an impact, and the Australian linked up well with Lampard, who was playing behind him. Within two minutes of the restart, the pair combined excellently to give Lampard the chance to strike from 25 yards, but he sent his shot wide.
But within a minute of the restart, Liverpool were in control. The ball was played down the left-hand side to the on-rushing Michael Owen, who crossed the ball for a waiting Kewell. He struck the ball well, with power, and with the accuracy of a man well used to scoring in big games, he placed the ball inside the near post at the expense of the visiting goalkeeper.
With Liverpool now on top, Rovers were finding it increasingly difficult to find any gaps in the Liverpool defence. The home team, however, had their own problems as they attempted to find a way past Friedel. The American goalkeeper, who was now playing well in the face of a barrage of shots from the Liverpool attack, was beaten once more when Crainey headed the ball across his goal and into the far corner.
The game was now wide open, and Liverpool continued to press for an equaliser. Gerrard struck the ball wide from the edge of the area, and a Kewell effort was then blocked by a defender.
The first substitution of the game came in the 65th minute, when Liverpool brought on Nick Barmby for Michael Owen, and the game now became a more even affair, as both teams searched for a winning goal.
With 20 minutes remaining, Liverpool again took the lead. Gary McAllister, playing in his 1000th game, picked up the ball in midfield and passed it to Gerrard. The redshirt captain then played it to Crainey, who was running down the right-hand side. He crossed the ball into the area, where Kewell, who had now moved to the left-hand side, was waiting. He met the ball with a header, which dropped into the far corner of the Rovers goal.
A minute later, Liverpool were awarded a corner, but the visitors defence was strong and it was not until the 88th minute that the ball fell to Kewell in the area. He struck the ball, but it was one of his weaker efforts, and Friedel saved easily.
With the game entering its final stages, Liverpool looked dangerous every time they attacked, and a late goal looked likely. However, it was the visitors who had the last chance of the game. Marcus Hahnemann, who had been long-serving substitute John Arne Riise, saved well from an effort from the visitors, and there was no further immediate danger as Liverpool held on for the win.
The game was a worthy contest and one that was rewarding for the fans who had come out on this uncharacteristically mild afternoon. It was a fitting tribute to Gary McAllister, who had made 1000 appearances, and, with the game now over, the redshirt man was applauded off the pitch by the Liverpool faithful.
In this game, Liverpool proved they can win without a potent attack and can also win with a team effort. In the past, the club have been criticised for the lack of a potent attack, but this match showed the players had the ability to overcome adversity and produce the goods when needed.

This defeat of the Qedarites by the Hittites, combined with the fall of the Kassite dynasty in Babylon, provided an opportunity for the Elamite Empire to expand its influence in the area, which it did by invading and occupying the land of Amurru. This is the background against which the story of Sinuhe is set, which is based on the Tale of a Shipwrecked Sailor from the 19th Dynasty. The storyline is presented here in the form which it took after the 18th Dynasty, in which the Egyptian protagonist is Sinuhe the Elder, son of Shen, who is in service at the court of the pharaoh, Amenhotep I. The story is told in the first person, and the main plot follows the journey of Sinuhe from Egypt, where he receives the news of his father's death, to the land of Canaan/Phoenicia. The story of Sinuhe is preserved in a papyrus scroll which was found by George Reisner in the tomb of a scribe in the 'Royal Tombs' at Thebes. This scribe, Khaemwast, was an overseer of scribes in the temple of Amun and the father of the famous scribe and historian, Manetho, who is credited with the creation of the first known history of Egypt, the Aegyptiaca.
In a previous incarnation, Sinuhe was the court physician to the pharaoh, Amenhotep I, and it is during this time that he is said to have written a book, 'The Doctrine of the Hundred Sections', which is dedicated to the goddess Hathor. The physician in this story is identified as Sinuhe's son, who inherits his father's profession. Sinuhe is described as being a member of the court nobility and a friend of the pharaoh, and his son is also said to have been a noble, though this is not made clear.
The story of Sinuhe is a work of fiction, but the historical background is authentic. The story was originally written in the form of a novel, but has been set out here in the narrative of the original, in the style of a chronicle. The story itself covers events taking place between the reigns of Amenhotep I and Thutmose III. There are several references to the sojourn of an Egyptian official at the court of the Hittite king, Alaksandus, in the reign of Thutmose III. We also know that the Egyptian king, Amenhotep III, sent his son, Amenhotep IV, on a diplomatic mission to the court of the Hittite king, Suppiluliuma I. The story of Sinuhe includes a reference to these events.
The original story, written in Middle Egyptian of the 17th Dynasty ( c. 1555–1535 BCE), was translated into Greek shortly after the time of Alexander the Great. This translation has been lost but its style and language can be seen in later versions of the story. It was rendered into English by E. A. Wallis Budge, who also supplied the present translation.

British search and rescue teams were the first to arrive in Léogane , the town at the epicenter of the quake , on 17 January .

12 were only 35 of the 100 or so survivors still alive when the British arrived.  Twelve days later, on 29 January, the United States Navy arrived in Haiti.  The Commander of the U.S. Southern Command, Admiral James Stavridis , said that "today, we are ready to take on our next task: the relief effort."  The United States Combatant Commands, U.S. Transportation Command , and U.S. Southern Command worked together to coordinate the relief effort.
The initial rescue efforts were in Léogâne , a city of 200,000 people about 30 miles (48 km) west of the capital, Port-au-Prince. On the second day of the rescue effort, a U.S. Air Force C-130 Hercules flew over Léogâne. It crashed, killing 15 Americans on board and 5 civilians on the ground. The victims were from the 82nd Airborne Division's 82nd Combat Aviation Brigade.  The airfield they were attempting to land on was previously cleared by a U.S. Marine Corps CH-53E Super Stallion. The crash of the C-130 was the largest single loss of life for the U.S. military in the disaster.  The incident was the first time that the 82nd Airborne Division was deployed in combat since the Korean War.  The Air Force launched a criminal investigation into the crash.  Along with the 15 people killed in the crash, 21 were injured, 10 of them seriously.
 In addition to U.S. military assets, the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) sent 8,000 military personnel to Haiti to co-ordinate the relief effort and to ensure the safety of U.S. personnel.  The DoD sent personnel from the U.S. Army, the U.S. Navy, the U.S. Marine Corps, and the U.S. Air Force.  The majority of the 8,000 DoD personnel were sent to Haiti from the United States Southern Command.  The 2nd Marine Expeditionary Force (2nd MEF) from Camp Lejeune , NC was the first unit deployed to Haiti.  The 2nd MEF was responsible for establishing a temporary airfield and port for U.S. military flights and ships.  The 3rd Marine Expeditionary Force from Okinawa, Japan and the 1st Battalion, 7th Marines from Camp Pendleton, California were also deployed to Haiti.  The 10th Mountain Division (Light) from Fort Drum, New York was also deployed to Haiti.  The 82nd Airborne Division from Fort Bragg, North Carolina was also deployed to Haiti.  The Combined Joint Task Force – Haiti (CJTF-H) was established at Port-au-Prince and was led by Brigadier General Kenrick C. Kieth.  The CJTF-H was responsible for coordinating the U.S. military's response to the earthquake in Haiti.  The USNS Comfort landed in Haiti on 28 January.  The Comfort was equipped with a hospital, operating rooms, and a helicopter deck.  The Comfort was used to treat victims of the earthquake and to provide medical evacuations (medevacs).  The Comfort was the first American hospital ship to visit Haiti in more than 10 years.  The ship had been called in by the U.S. President, Barack Obama, to aid in the earthquake relief effort.  The ship had more than 1200 medical personnel on board.  In addition to the USNS Comfort, the U.S. Coast Guard, the U.S. Navy, and U.S. Marine Corps were also deployed to Haiti.  The Coast Guard, Navy, and Marine Corps were responsible for search and rescue, humanitarian aid, and port security.  The Coast Guard, Navy, and Marine Corps were also responsible for medical evacuations with helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.
The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) was also involved in the Haiti earthquake relief effort.  The USAID deployed teams to Haiti to assess the damage caused by the earthquake.  The USAID was also involved in distributing food and water to victims of the earthquake.

riered the message to the sloop ahead: " The Ship is in Sight! " The order to run past Africaine had been given with perfect timing; the seamen on the little sloop had no time to react.
At last the two ships were alongside, and the sailors could see that Otter and Staunch had been given a thorough beating. Boadicea was damaged too, but the fighting had been fierce enough to have slowed her down by a few thousand yards. It was now 18 : 25 .
The commander of Africaine had been in contact with the Submarine Commanders Headquarters at Plymouth, and with the Admiralty. The orders were clear: sink the German raider at all costs.
The first thing to do, however, was to establish the strength of the raider's crew and guns. At first the Germans on board Africaine did not even know whether the raider was a cruiser or a destroyer, and the captain of Africaine did not know whether she had guns or not.
Africaine's 120 mm guns were trained on the raider, but, as the ships were so close, the Germans on board the raider could clearly see what was happening. They had their own 15 cm guns trained on Africaine, and, as the tiny sloop was already under way, they were confident they could sink the little vessel if they fired.
The captain of the raider knew he had to see what was happening on Africaine's decks, but he was too close to risk a boarding party. At last, at 18 : 30 , two men in the raider's bows, one in a red shirt and the other in a white shirt, were seen. They were clearly identifiable as officers, and the German captain was able to send a message to Africaine to tell the captain that he had two officers on board.
It was now 18 : 35 . The Germans were not to know that the two men in those "red" and "white" shirts were in fact Lieutenants Boyle, of the Royal Navy, and Holman, of the RAF, who were in fact wearing civilian clothing.
The captain of the raider was now convinced that Africaine was a cruiser, and he wanted to know whether he could fire on her. The captain of Africaine had no choice but to answer in the affirmative. The German captain had been determined to sink Africaine, and now he gave the order to open fire. The order was given with a quick nod of the head, and a second later, the two 15 cm guns went off almost simultaneously.
The first shell tore a great hole in Africaine's hull, and the second hit the bridge and killed the captain and the first officer. The third shell struck the ship's radio shack and killed the wireless operator and another man. The fourth shell hit the deckhouse and killed the ship's carpenter. The fifth shell struck the funnel and killed two men.
The sixth shell killed a man in the engine room. The seventh shell hit the deckhouse and killed another man.
The next shell hit the bridge and struck the captain in the head. (He would die later in the Royal Naval Hospital at Haslar.) The captain of Africaine had to be knocked down by one of the men on the bridge. When the captain came to he found himself on the floor, with a man standing over him.
The man was a first-class fireman, and he was holding a smoke helmet in his hand.
"Get up, Sir , " the fireman said. "I'm the new captain."
The captain was still dazed by the attack, and tried to focus on the man standing over him. The man was wearing white overalls, and the captain asked the man to remove his overalls.
The man obeyed, and the captain saw the red shirt and yellow star of the RAF under the man's white shirt. It was then that the captain realized that the entire crew of Africaine was in disguise.
The German raider had been suppressed, and the two ships, now without their captains, dropped anchor.

The Chapel of the Holy Angels and Archangels ( Spanish : Capilla de los Ángeles ) was finished in 1665 with Baroque altarpieces

[ citation needed ] and is located in the Basilica of Our Lady of the Angels ( Spanish : Basílica de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles ) in Los Angeles, California, built in the 1820s. 

## Description

The chapel is located in the upper church near the altar of the Virgin of the Angels, on the right side of the Basilica . A special feature of the chapel is that the altarpiece is located on the left side of the chapel. The Chapel of the Holy Angels and Archangels is dedicated to Archangel Michael, Archangel Gabriel and Archangel Raphael. The 15th century fresco of the Archangels is located in the vault of the chapel. The pictorial cycle of the Archangels is from 1850 and is located behind the altar. 

## The Chapel of the Holy Angels and Archangels in popular culture

In the 1990s, the music group The Red Hot Chili Peppers shot a music video for their single "The Power of Equality" at the Chapel of the Holy Angels and Archangels.

The aim of the book is to show that such a discrepancy exists, and to prove it with the aid of a computer-assisted analysis. In his introduction , the author explains that he started to use the computer to solve this problem , because he was not able to answer the question himself. The problem is the following :
Definition: an opening is effective if White has a positive score in a large number of games.
The author claims that the evaluation of these openings is not as simple as it seems. He gives the example of the Caro-Kann Defense, an opening that has a large number of games that start with 1.e4 c6. The score of White in these games is about 60 percent. The same applies to the Queen's Gambit Declined, Ruy Lopez and Sicilian Defense. The problem (in the author's words) is that " on a superficial level, the score of White in these openings looks to be very good."

The 2nd Devons arrived at 08 : 15 , while the beach was still under heavy fire . One company stayed to help with the assault on

the eastern end of the beach and the other two moved on the western end as soon as the beach was secured . During this time, the commanding officer of the 7th Brigade, Colonel F. L. Etherington, was hit by a bullet and died of his wounds .
 At 10 : 15 the queue of men and vehicles waiting to get off the beach stretched back for over 1,500 yd, and was moving forward at a rate of about 50 yd per hour . The beach was no longer under direct fire, but it had been reduced to a quagmire by the shelling .
 Some units were held up for some time by mines and obstacles, notably the 56th Division at La Rabière, where the destroyer _Wakeful_ was sunk by a mine . The 2nd Devons were held up by a minefield and a large number of obstacles, some of which had to be cleared by the minesweepers _Lydd_ and _Brighton_.
 The Luftwaffe tried to intervene but was driven off by the ships' anti-aircraft guns. At 11 : 10, the _Walcheren_ , one of the naval support vessels, was hit and set on fire .
 By 11 : 45 most of the troops and vehicles had been ferried to the shore. The beach was still under indirect fire and there were still some obstacles to clear, but the situation was under control.

series , from the cinematography to the editing , to the special effects , to the use of the score , to the design of the characters , has been treated with the same care and craft that goes into a major motion picture ."

According to the network, the series "is the most visually stylized drama series ever produced by television, and it looks every bit as good as it feels."

## Production

### Development

In July 2014, Fox ordered the series to pilot. The pilot was written by Charlie Eglee and directed by Omar Madha.

In October 2014, Fox ordered the series to series.

### Casting

In October 2014, it was announced that Michael Ealy would star in the series. The series would be executive produced and co-starred by Sarah Allen, Mimi Kirkland, Chris Galya, and Jill E. Alexander. In November 2014, it was announced that Shane West, Megalyn E.K., and Anne Winters would co-star in the series. In December 2014, it was announced that Mary Elizabeth Winstead, Jessica Lucas and Brendan Meyer would co-star in the series.

### Filming

In November 2014, filming commenced for the series.

### Music

The soundtrack was released by Lakeshore Records on November 6, 2015. It features the song "Girl Ridin'" by Ellie Goulding.

## Reception

### Critical response

On Rotten Tomatoes the series has an approval rating of 43% based on 35 reviews with an average rating of 5.3/10. The site's critical consensus reads, "Chosen will please fans of the Scream franchise, but its lesser-than-expected quality reveals it to be a franchise on the wane." On Metacritic it has a score of 54 out of 100, based on 12 critics, indicating "mixed or average reviews".

Tel Shiloh (Hebrew : תֵּל שְׁלוֹם , Arabic : اتِّل شِلْحُ ) is an archaeological site located in the Samarian foothills of the central West Bank , 1.5 km (0.93 mi) south of Shiloh .  The site is believed to have been the ancient city of Shiloh , the home of the Tabernacle in the time of the judges ,  and the first capital of the Kingdom of Israel .
In the Bible , the site is said to have been the burial place of the Patriarchs Jacob and Joseph .  The site is a holy site for the Samaritans , who believe that it was the original location of the Temple of the Israelites .  The site is known to have been inhabited from the Chalcolithic  period ,  the Bronze Age ,  and the Iron Age , and is believed to have been destroyed by the Babylonians . According to the Bible, the site was destroyed at the end of the reign of Jeroboam II when the Israelites were taken captive to Assyria .
Some scholars believe that the site of Tel Shiloh is unrelated to the biblical city of Shiloh.  Others believe that the site is the biblical Shiloh. Vocal political dissidents opposed to Portuguese rule and claiming independence were typically forced into exile . From the mid

-17th century, many of them found refuge in the Dutch Republic, where they organized into associations and clubs. The most prominent ones were the Brotherhood of the Rosary (brotherhood of the rosa) in Amsterdam and the Brotherhood of the Red Star (brotherhood of the estrela vermelha) in Leiden.
The Portuguese settlers in the Dutch Republic were the subjects of a unique system of government that gave them more autonomy and privileges than what was typical in the Dutch Republic. The privileges included the right to set up their own schools, churches, and charities. They were also not required to pay taxes or to serve in the Dutch army.
The Brotherhood of the Rosary was founded in Amsterdam in 1642 and was open to all Portuguese men and women of the Dutch Republic. The Brotherhood of the Red Star was founded in Leiden in 1657 and was open only to men.
The two brotherhoods had great influence on the organization of the Portuguese clandestine against the Portuguese colonial authorities.

The Battle of Milne Bay, fought over a five-day period in September 1942, was the first major battle between the Japanese and the Allies in the south-west Pacific. It was also the first time the Japanese had fought a battle in the tropics, and the Australians were able to make use of the knowledge they had gained on the Kokoda Trail. The battle was a great victory for the Allies, but for the Japanese it was a disaster.
Air Marshal Sutherland's report to the Australian Minister of Defence, dated October 2, 1942.
MY DEAR SIR
I have the honour to report:
The fight at Milne Bay was one of the most successful and gallant that has been fought by our forces in the Pacific Campaign. The enemy was defeated with very small losses to us.
The success of the operation was due to the support given by the RAAF. The Australian 7th Division, with the addition of the 26th Brigade, mounted a splendid attack on an enemy that had entrenched itself in well-built trenches and had the advantage of the jungle. The Australians, however, soon overcame these advantages and went on to capture the objectives.
The enemy lost a large number of men and material. This was probably the most decisive battle of the war in the South West Pacific.
I wish to record my appreciation to all concerned, particularly the staff of the 7th Division.
The Australians are the best soldiers in the world.
 Yours sincerely, ARTHUR G. SUTHERLAND,
AIR MARSHAL.

" Yo @-@ Yo " is a 1950s @-@ themed electropop and synthpop song in which Roberts sings about an undecided lover . The song rec

alls Roberts ' early work in the 1980s, which was heavily influenced by the synth-pop sound of the era .

## Background

The song was written by Roberts and his longtime collaborator Dan Owen, who also contributed the song's music. According to Roberts, the song was based on a real-life experience dating an undecided lover. The song's lyrics are largely ambiguous and reflect this theme. The song's lyrics include "Yo, yo, yeah, yeah, I'm gonna make you understand, " and "Yo, yo, yeah, yeah, let me hit you up again, " suggesting that the love interest is unsure if they want to be with the singer .

The song's music video was directed by David Mould . The video premiered on May 16, 2022, and was filmed at the Royal Academy of Arts in London, England . The video begins with Roberts in a large gallery, surrounded by artwork. He then walks through the gallery, interacting with the artworks and exhibits. The video then transitions to scenes of the singer in a recording studio, where he is seen performing the song. The video concludes with Roberts in the gallery, surrounded by the artwork that he interacted with earlier in the video.

## Critical reception

Roberts performing the song at Alexandra Palace

The song received positive reviews from music critics. Tom Breihan of Stereogum called the song a "gloriously fun" neon-lit dance track, while also comparing it to Roberts's early work in the 1980s. Mike Wass of Idolator described the song as "retro-futuristic" and "dance-pop". Wass also praised the song's production and its "cheeky, throwback" vibe, and called it "a triumphant return to form".

The powerful Kievan state was founded in the 9th century, and the Kievan Rus was a single, united state which existed until the middle of the 13th century. This state was followed by the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, which included Ukraine and part of Belarus, and the state of the Grand Duchy of Moscow, which included Russia. The Grand Duchy of Lithuania was founded by the Lithuanian duke, Gediminas, in 1323.
In the 14th century, Ukraine began to develop as an independent state. During most of this period, however, the Grand Duchy of Lithuania controlled the lands of Ukraine. In the 16th century, Ukraine was conquered by the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. In 1648, the Cossacks, who were subordinates of the Polish nobles, took part in rebellion against the Polish government. This rebellion lasted from 1648 to 1654 and was known as the Zaporozhian Cossack Uprising. The Cossacks won the war, and Ukraine became independent. This marked the beginning of the Ukrainian period in the history of Ukraine.
The Ukrainian period in the history of Ukraine began with the Zaporozhian Cossack Uprising.
After the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth lost the War with Sweden (1655-1660), Ukraine became a part of the Russian Empire . This period was known as the period of Russian rule in Ukraine. During this period, Ukraine was known as a province of Imperial Russia . This ended in 1917, when Ukraine became independent.

This vegetation type is usually associated with rocky slopes and provides food for the endangered Cape rockjumper ( Gerygone igata ).

The Johnson – Corey – Chaykovsky reaction ( sometimes referred to as the Corey – Chaykovsky reaction or CCR ) is a chemical rea

ction in which an aldehyde is reduced to an alcohol and a nitroso compound by a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas. The name is derived from the names of the three chemists who independently developed the reaction in the 1960s: James S. Johnson , Robert W. Chayovsky and, independently, Vladimir V. Corey . 

Corey–Chayovsky

## Background

In 1967, the catalytic hydrogenation of aldehydes was accomplished by the use of a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas, in the presence of a catalyst and a complexing agent (primarily phosphines, triphenylphosphine or bis(triphenylphosphine)palladium(0) ).

## Mechanism

The catalytic hydrogenation of several aldehydes, including benzaldehyde, to their corresponding alcohols by a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas has been reported.

The dehydrogenation of alpha-thioacetates to aldehydes was accomplished by a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas in the presence of a catalyst and a complexing agent (primarily phosphines, triphenylphosphine, or bis(triphenylphosphine)palladium(0) ).

### General

The CCR uses a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas to reduce aldehydes to alcohols and nitroso compounds.

The catalytic hydrogenation of several aldehydes, including benzaldehyde, to their corresponding alcohols by a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas has been reported.

The dehydrogenation of alpha-thioacetates to aldehydes was accomplished by a catalytic amount of hydrogen gas in the presence of a catalyst and a complexing agent (primarily phosphines, triphenylphosphine, or bis(triphenylphosphine)palladium(0) ).

### Organozinc

The CCR with organozinc reagents (RMgX or R'MgX) is considered to be a variant of the CCR.

### Example

The CCR using diallylzinc (Zn(C(CH₃)₂)₂) as the catalyst in combination with triphosphine and phosphine oxide, in the presence of a stoichiometric amount of aldehyde in benzene CCR) was used to reduce alpha-thioacetates to the corresponding aldehydes in good to excellent yields.

## Scope

The CCR can be used to reduce aldehydes to alcohols and nitroso compounds.

The CCR with organozinc reagents (RMgX or R'MgX) is considered to be a variant of the CCR.

The CCR using diallylzinc (Zn(C(CH₃)₂)₂) as the catalyst in combination with triphosphine and phosphine oxide, in the presence of a stoichiometric amount of aldehyde in benzene CCR) was used to reduce alpha-thioacetates to the corresponding aldehydes in good to excellent yields.

Having previously worked on D.R. & Quinch for 2000 AD , a title made popular by John Constantine 's creator Alan Moore , Delano

decided to revive the character and the title.
After this initial period, the series was cancelled by publisher Rebellion, although Delano himself has said that he has not abandoned the character, and that he has plans for him.
The first four stories feature the character Quinch, a giant, green, foul-mouthed, and foul-smelling alien from the planet Quingq. His companion is a small, red alien named Dimi, who is also Quinch's archenemy (and Dimi's planet, Kling, is Quingq's enemy). Both aliens are bounty hunters, working for the Space Police. In the first storyline, they are sent to Earth to track down a trio of aliens who have stolen a spaceship, but when they arrive, they discover that the aliens are undercover, bent on investigating Earth. In the second storyline, the pair are sent to the planet Kling, where they are captured by the Space Police and sentenced to death for murder. They escape and find that the local bounty hunters are also being hunted, and they are the only ones who can save them.
In the third storyline, Quinch and Dimi are sent to the planet Gling to investigate the disappearance of a space-faring race that has been missing for centuries. The pair are captured by the Gling, who believe them to be spies and set out to find out who they really are.
The final storyline sees the pair captured by a race of aliens who are planning to use them as a means of transporting a dangerous weapon called the 'Sand-at-ma-gus' to Earth.
The series was later reprinted by Marvel UK in 1995 , and in 2019 by Rebellion Publishing .
The stories were written by Peter Hogan , and illustrated by Lee Sullivan .
Quinch and Dimi was nominated for the Eagle Award for Best Comic in 2001.

L. indigo is a mycorrhizal fungus , and as such , establishes a mutualistic relationship with the roots of certain trees ( " ho

yas " in English ). An important symbiosis is that of the rain tree, which provides to the fungus the nitrogen necessary for its development.
L. indigo is present in tropical regions of the world such as Africa, the Philippines, Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, the American Caribbean, Central and South America (the Amazon basin).

It was involved in the fighting on the Kokoda Track in New Guinea in late 1942 and early 1943, eventually being withdrawn to Port Moresby for rest and recreation. After the Japanese surrender, the battalion returned to Australia in March 1945, being disbanded on 14 July 1945.

any real understanding of their essence. The literary sources of Jainism and their writings were unimaginable without the understanding of these two concepts. What was the significance of the eternal union of these two terms and how did the meaning of anekāntavāda and syādvāda get transmitted in Jainism and how did they evolve in time? In this chapter, I will first discuss their evolution in early Jainism and then in the modern age with the help of the Jain scriptures.
The term anekāntavāda was first used in a Jain context in the _Uttarapurāṇa_. In the _Uttarapurāṇa_ , anekāntavāda is used in the context of the _sutra_ , ' _Ekāntamantramanushayam'_. _Sūtra_ means 'sentence.' This sentence, _ekāntamantramanushayam_ , is one of the most important and significant sentences in Jain _Bhagavat_ literature. It is also the most important sentence in _lokdharma_ , the Jain cosmology. In the _Bhagavat literature_ , this sentence is also called the _ekānta-vṛtti_ ('sentence of unity'). The sentence is used in many _Vārṣabhānavṛtti_ (discourses) written by the _Bhagavat_ s and in the _Tattvārthasaṃgraha_ (comprehensive treatise on logic and ontology) written by _Bhagavat_ s. The sentence states that the _sat_ (reality), which is one, is present in different forms and is called different names in different contexts. The sentence _ekāntamantramanushayam_ is a very important sentence in Jain cosmology.
The sentence, _ekāntamantramanushayam_ , is mentioned in verse 15 of the twenty-third chapter of the _Bhagavat_ _Purāṇa_ (chapter 23, verse 15). It is also mentioned in verse 10 of the twenty-fourth chapter of the _Bhagavat_ _Purāṇa_ (chapter 24, verse 10).
The _Uttarapurāṇa_ is the only text where the term 'anekāntavāda' is used in the context of the _sutra_ , ' _Ekāntamantramanushayam_ '.
As far as the concept of anekāntavāda is concerned, the _Sūtra_ _Prabhāsottara_ has a beautiful verse. This verse is also well known in Jain literature and is quoted by many authors. It is found in verse 11 of the chapter on ' _Dravyadvaya_ ' in the _Sūtra_ _Prabhāsottara_ (chapter 11, verse 11).
The term 'syādvāda' is not mentioned in the _Uttarapurāṇa_ in the context of the _sutra_ , ' _Ekāntamantramanushayam_ '. The word 'syādvāda' is used in the _Bhagavat_ literature for the first time in verse 10 of the twenty-third chapter of the _Bhagavat_ _Purāṇa_ (chapter 23, verse 10).
As far as the concept of syādvāda is concerned, the _Sūtra_ _Prabhāsottara_ has a beautiful verse in verse 36 of the chapter on ' _Dravyadvaya_ '.

The South Carolina State Museum in Columbia houses the world's largest collection of sharks' teeth.
The two most famous shark teeth are the Megalodon, the largest shark to ever exist, and the Mosasaur. Mosasaurs were ancient aquatic reptiles that looked like crocodiles, but had the body shape of a shark.

In the chronic stage , treatment involves managing the clinical manifestations of the disease . For example , pacemakers and me

chano-electrical therapies are sometimes used to manage arrhythmias . In addition , various medications are used to treat the clinical manifestations of advanced heart failure .
Some people with heart failure may experience shortness of breath with minimal activity ; for these patients , a prostaglandin inhibitor (such as ibutilide , amiodarone , or dobutamine ) may be used to improve exercise ability .
In addition , a number of medications are used for their anti-inflammatory effects . For example , the non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications , such as sulindac , are sometimes used for their effects on the inflammatory response .
In addition , a number of medications are used for the treatment of advanced heart failure . For example , the use of bevacizumab , an anti-angiogenesis agent , may improve heart function and reduce heart failure symptoms in patients with advanced heart failure .
 Finally , the use of cardiac resynchronization therapy may improve heart function in patients with advanced heart failure .

Medications may also be used for the management of the symptoms of heart failure .

### Cardiac surgery

Cardiac surgery is sometimes used for the management of severe symptoms of heart failure .

### Heart transplantation

Heart transplantation may be used for the management of severe symptoms of heart failure .

### Assist devices

Heart failure may be treated with ventricular assist devices (VADs). This type of device may be used as a bridge to transplantation, as an alternative to a transplant or as a way to prolong a transplant.

## Prevention

While there is no way to prevent heart failure, lifestyle changes can help to reduce the risk of developing or exacerbating heart failure. This includes eating a healthy diet, exercising, and stopping smoking.

It is unclear how many species of Allosaurus there were . Eight species have been considered potentially valid since 1988 ( A.

macintoshi, A. fragilis, A. amplus, A. fragilis, A. jimmadseni, A. novae, A. jurassicus, and A. ferrragoensis). The validity of several of these is disputed by some paleontologists. Several other species were named in the 19th and early 20th centuries, but they are now considered invalid, and their names so far have not been reassigned to any of the valid species.
Allosaurus was one of a group of large theropod dinosaurs called the megalosaurids, which were the dominant predators in Jurassic North America. It was a member of the family Allosauridae, which includes the more basal genera Antrodemus, Syntarsus, and Telmatosaurus. Allosaurus was larger than most other theropods, with an estimated length of 9 m (30 ft), and a weight of about 2 tons (1.8 tonnes).
Allosaurus is known from a diverse fossil record that includes skeletons of almost complete individuals. It was a quadrupedal predator with a long, heavy tail. It had sharp, curved claws on each foot and a powerful bite, adapted for attacking prey.
Allosaurus lived between 155 and 145 million years ago, during the Late Jurassic period. It is known to have coexisted with stegosaurs, sauropods, ceratopsians, and other theropods.
The type species A. fragilis was named by the American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877. A. macintoshi was named by the American paleontologist Charles Whitney Gilmore in 1926, and A. novae was named by the American paleontologist James I. Kirkland in 1994. The genus name Allosaurus combines the Greek words allos, meaning "other", and sauros, meaning "lizard" . The species name fragilis means "fragile" .
Allosaurus was one of the best-known and most-studied dinosaurs during the early twentieth century. In 1988, the American paleontologist James A. Jensen published a phylogenetic analysis of theropod dinosaurs, in which he included Allosaurus. He found that it was a basal member of the group Megalosauridae. He considered A. macintoshi to be a valid species, and named a second species, A. fragilis, to distinguish it from the type species A. fragilis . Later phylogenetic analyses, such as those of Matthew Carrano in 1998, David B. Weishampel in 2004, and Gregory S. Paul in 2010, recovered Allosaurus in a more basal position, outside of Megalosauridae.
Allosaurus is known from fossils found in the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of North America, apart from the type species, which is known from the Tecovas Formation of Texas. The type species was described from fossil remains found near Fruitland, Wyoming, and named by Marsh in 1877. In 1979, paleontologist Robert T. Bakker suggested that A. fragilis was a separate species from A. fragilis, and in 1988, Jensen erected the new species A. macintoshi. A. jimmadseni was named by James Kirkland in 1994 from fossils found near Jensen, Utah, and A. novae was named by James Kirkland in 1994 from fossils found near the town of Novae, Utah.
Allosaurus was a medium-sized theropod, slightly larger than Tyrannosaurus . The holotype skeleton of A. fragilis was about 9 m (30 ft) long. It is about 80% the size of the 10-metre (33 ft) long Brachiosaurus, which was the longest dinosaur known at the time of its description. The holotype skeleton of A. macintoshii was about 7.5 m (25 ft) long. It is about 70% the size of the 10-metre (33 ft) long Brachiosaurus, which was the longest dinosaur known at the time of its description. The holotype skeleton of A. jimmadseni was about 8 m (26 ft) long

The 1976–77 season was Chelsea's most successful season to date. In the league, Chelsea finished second, only 2 points behind Liverpool. The new capital Hangzhou grew into a major commercial and cultural center . It rose from a middling city of no special importan

ce in the 11th century to the most important city in the four southern provinces of China by the 14th century. Presiding over the city was the West Lake, a jewel of a lake with many interesting sights and a host of temples and gardens. The West Lake became the famous romantic lake of Chinese literature, and Hangzhou was the city of poets.
During the Ming and Qing Dynasties (1368–1911), Hangzhou remained a center of culture and learning. The Yue opera, which was performed in Hangzhou, was one of the most popular of the Chinese operas. The Qing Dynasty's poet, Li Bai, wrote the famous poem "Boat on the Lake". The famous Chinese writer, Huang Dafu, was born in Hangzhou.
During the Republic of China period (1912–1949), Hangzhou remained a center of culture and learning. The end of the Republic of China period was the beginning of the People's Republic of China (PRC). After the establishment of the PRC, Hangzhou was the capital city of Zhejiang Province.
In 1997, Hangzhou became the capital of the Zhejiang Province and was also selected as a national central city. In 2000, it was officially named one of China's four ancient capitals.
The Hangzhou Metropolitan Area is the economical core of Zhejiang, and has become an important hub for revolutionary industry and commerce. It has the third largest GDP in China.
With its history of over 2,000 years, Hangzhou is a city with a rich culture.
Hangzhou has a population of 7.9 million, and the total area of the city is 16,598 square kilometers (6,405 sq mi).
Hangzhou is located in the center of Zhejiang Province, adjacent to the Yangtze River Delta. It is about 100 kilometers (62 mi) from the coast.
The city is divided into five districts, namely, Xihu, Jianggan, Binjiang, Yuhang, and Xiaoshan. Xihu is the core area of the city. Jianggan, Binjiang, Yuhang, and Xiaoshan are all suburban districts.
The city is situated in the transitional area between the North China Plain and the south. The Hangzhou Plain is in the middle of the city. The elevation varies from 18 meters (59 ft) to 100 meters (330 ft).
The four main rivers of Hangzhou are Qiantang River and Xin'an River, and their tributaries are Yue Creek and Qiantang River. The northern part of the city is drained by Qiantang River and its tributaries. The southern part of the city is drained by the Xin'an River and its tributaries.
Hangzhou has a humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification Cwa), with four distinct seasons.
Winter is mild, with average temperatures around 6 °C (43 °F).
Summer is hot and humid, with average temperatures around 27 °C (81 °F).
Spring and autumn are mild, with average temperatures around 15 °C (59 °F).
Hangzhou has a long history of heavy rainfall. It has a high humidity year-round, and monsoons and typhoons come from the South China Sea.
The Qiantang River in Hangzhou is known for its tide, which is one of the biggest tides in the world.
Hangzhou was the capital of the Southern Song Dynasty from 1127 to 1279, the Zhejiang-Jiangxi Republic from 1912 to 1913, and the Republic of China from 1913 to 1927.

After the end of World War II, Hangzhou was again the capital of Zhejiang Province.

The Atlantic hurricane season officially began on June 15 , 1955 . It was an above average season in which 13 tropical cyclones

developed in the basin . The first storm to develop was Hurricane Connie . It was a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir–Simpson hurricane scale . It strengthened to a Category 5 hurricane on the day it struck North Carolina on September 13, 1955 . After the storm weakened to a Category 4 hurricane, it struck the Outer Banks of North Carolina. It caused 53 fatalities and $17 million in damage in its path. Connie was the first hurricane of the season to strike the United States since Hurricane Audrey in 1957 . The last storm to form was Hurricane Ophelia . It hit the United States on September 12, 1955 . It was a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir–Simpson hurricane scale . After the storm weakened to a Category 3 hurricane, it struck the Outer Banks of North Carolina. It caused 19 fatalities and $18 million in damage in its path. Ophelia was the last storm of the season to strike the United States.
Throughout the season, a total of 22 National Weather Service (NWS) sites recorded tropical cyclone rainfall amounts. The highest rainfall total reported was 11.13 inches (283 mm) in Buxton, North Carolina that occurred as a result of Hurricane Connie. Other rainfall amounts reported by NWS sites were 7.5 inches (190 mm) in Cherry Grove, North Carolina, 3.6 inches (91 mm) in Bermuda, 2.4 inches (61 mm) in St. Augustine, Florida, and 2.0 inches (51 mm) in St. George's, Bermuda.
Throughout the season, a total of 26 National Weather Service (NWS) sites reported tropical cyclone wind gusts. The highest wind gust reported was 116 mph (187 km/h) in Portsmouth, Virginia that occurred as a result of Hurricane Ophelia. Other wind gusts reported by NWS sites were 87 mph (140 km/h) in Norfolk, Virginia, 62 mph (100 km/h) in Charleston, South Carolina, 52 mph (84 km/h) in Wilmington, North Carolina, 40 mph (64 km/h) in St. Augustine, Florida, and 38 mph (61 km/h) in Jacksonville, Florida.
Throughout the season, a total of 27 National Weather Service (NWS) sites reported tropical cyclone storm surge. The highest storm surge reported was 12.0 feet (3.7 m) in Buxton, North Carolina that occurred as a result of Hurricane Connie. Other storm surge reports by NWS sites were 8.8 feet (2.7 m) in Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina, 3.8 feet (1.2 m) in Charleston, South Carolina, 2.5 feet (0.8 m) in Norfolk, Virginia, 2.0 feet (0.6 m) in Cape Canaveral, Florida, and 1.5 feet (0.5 m) in Jacksonville, Florida.

Jon Favreau (born October 19, 1966) is an American actor, director, producer and screenwriter. He is of Italian, Hungarian, English, Spanish, and French ancestry.
Favreau was born in Flushing, Queens, New York City, the son of Madeleine (née Kuckenberg) and Charles Favreau. His father worked as an executive for the accounting firm of Arthur Andersen. His mother was a speech teacher. Favreau is a 1984 graduate of Stuyvesant High School in Manhattan. He attended the University of Southern California School of Cinematic Arts and graduated in 1990.
Favreau first became known as a writer, beginning with his screenplay for Rudy (1993). He has also written and produced numerous films, including Elf (2003), Zathura: A Space Adventure (2005), Iron Man (2008), Iron Man 2 (2010), Cowboys & Aliens (2011), and the third and fourth films in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Iron Man 3 (2013) and Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015). He directed the first two films. He also wrote and produced the first two seasons of the television series Daredevil.
Favreau has appeared in numerous films, including Swingers (1996), Very Bad Things (1998), Couples Retreat (2009), and Chef (2014). He also starred in the sitcom Dads (2013–2014). He directed the live-action remakes of The Jungle Book (2016) and The Lion King (2019).
Favreau has directed the first two films in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Iron Man (2008) and Iron Man 2 (2010). He reprised the role as director for the Marvel-produced film Cowboys & Aliens (2011). Favreau is also well-known for his role as Happy Hogan in the Iron Man series, and will reprise that role in Iron Man 3 (2013), Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015) and Avengers: Infinity War (2018).
Favreau and his wife, Erica Hill, have two children, Max Favreau (born 2001) and Madeleine Favreau (born 2003).

ical Force during the Second World War. A unit of the 1st Armoured Division, the 2/4th MGB was formed in April 1941 at Seymour, Victoria. From April 1941 until June 1943, the 2/4th MGB was based in Australia, training for service in the Pacific. After shipping to the Middle East in June 1943, the battalion underwent training in Palestine and Syria until December 1943, when it was dispatched to Greece. The unit spent three months in Greece before arriving in Italy, where it was assigned to the 16th Australian Infantry Brigade of the 7th Australian Division. The 2/4th MGB spent the majority of the Italian Campaign in the 16th Brigade's forward area, engaging in frequent patrols and ambushes. The 2/4th MGB remained in Italy until November 1944, when it was withdrawn to the United Kingdom, arriving in December 1944. After a period of leave, the unit returned to Australia in March 1945, arriving at Seymour, Victoria in April 1945. The 2/4th MGB was disbanded in July 1945.

### Formation and training

The 2/4th Machine Gun Battalion was formed in April 1941 at Seymour, Victoria. It was part of the all volunteer Second Australian Imperial Force. The battalion was initially commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Rupert Clyne OBE. The unit was initially formed as a machine gun unit, with three companies of 30 men each. Named for the two machine gun companies and the four companies of riflemen, it was later joined by a headquarters company, and a post exchange, supply and transport company.

The 2/4th MGB was one of 12 organised by the 8th Division in late 1940 and early 1941. The unit was intended to be a part of the 2nd Armoured Division. This division would have been made up of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Machine Gun Battalions. Due to the need for armoured units in the Middle East, the 2nd Armoured Division was formed separately and was planned to be sent to the Middle East with the 2nd Machine Gun Battalion acting as its armoured unit. This plan was changed in May 1941 due to the need for the division in the Pacific. The 2nd and 3rd Machine Gun Battalions were reorganised as infantry, and the 2nd Armoured Division was disbanded. In October 1941 the 1st and 4th Machine Gun Battalions were also reorganised as infantry, leaving the 2nd, 3rd and 8th Machine Gun Battalions as the only three remaining units.

The battalion was assigned to the 1st Armoured Division and based the 8th Division's headquarters at Haifa. The 2/4th MGB was reassigned to the 16th Australian Infantry Brigade in January 1942. In April 1942, the 2/4th MGB moved to Syria and was stationed in Damascus. From April to July 1942, the 2/4th MGB was part of the Australian 1st Armoured Division's advance into Syria. The ship was assigned to the 19th Destroyer Flotilla on the start of the war and spent the first six months on escort and patro

li duties. After the evacuation of Greece in April 1941, the flotilla was disbanded and the destroyers were based at Alexandria, Egypt. The ship, together with the other destroyers, was involved in anti-submarine patrols and escort duties in the Mediterranean. In May 1941, the ship was assigned to the 10th Destroyer Flotilla for convoy escort duties in the Mediterranean. In February 1942, the ship participated in Operation Compass, the Allied campaign against Italian forces in Libya. During the operation, the ship participated in the Battle of Beda Fomm on 27 February 1942. During the battle, the ship fired 200 rounds from her main battery and had to be towed by her sister ship HMS Ilex to Malta due to engine damage.

The ship was assigned to the 14th Destroyer Flotilla in March 1942. During the Battle of Matapan in March 1942, the ship was involved in the engagement with the Italian fleet. In July 1942, the ship and the 14th Destroyer Flotilla were involved in Operation Pedestal, which was the attempt to resupply Malta. During the operation, the ship was involved in the Battle of Cape Spada. The ship was badly damaged by the Italian torpedo boat Circe and was towed to Malta by HMS Hero. The ship was involved in the Battle of Sirte off the Libyan coast during the operation. After the ship was repaired, she returned to England.

In January 1943, the ship was assigned to the 18th Destroyer Flotilla. During the invasion of Sicily in July 1943, the ship was in the flotilla that landed the 8th Army on the island. During the invasion, the ship was involved in the battle for the port of Syracuse. She was involved in operations off the coast of Italy throughout the rest of the year. In March 1944, the ship was assigned to the 11th Destroyer Flotilla. During the invasion of Normandy in June 1944, the ship was one of the 20 destroyers that landed the 50th (Northumbrian) Infantry Division on the beaches of Juno. The ship was involved in bombardment of German positions before the landings and later provided naval gunfire support during the landings.

### Pacific

In September 1944, the ship was assigned to the 21st Destroyer Flotilla. In November 1944, the ship was sent to the Far East. The ship was assigned to the British Pacific Fleet and arrived at Singapore on 22 December 1944. The ship operated out of Trincomalee, Ceylon (modern day Sri Lanka) during the Burma campaign. In May 1945, the ship was assigned to the 2nd Destroyer Flotilla. During the Battle of Okinawa, the ship was involved in naval gunfire support throughout the campaign in the area. In May 1945, the ship was assigned to the 3rd Destroyer Flotilla and was involved in a number of operations against Japanese positions.

After the war, the ship was assigned to the 5th Destroyer Flotilla. In September 1945, the ship escorted the battleship HMS Nelson from Trincomalee to Malta.

### Post war

The ship was assigned to the 1st Destroyer Flotilla in March 1946 and remained in service with the Royal Navy until she was paid off in August 1946. The ship was then sold to the ship breakers and scrapped.
